channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports league sources “don’t foresee” QB Aaron Rodgers playing again, barring an injury-driven emergency.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers

Rodgers cleared waivers Thursday and no immediate suitors emerged. The 42-year-old free agent QB torched what was left of his Steelers career earlier this week when he issued an ultimatum to Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, got benched, appeared on the Pat McAfee Show and was released. Plenty of teams are missing their starting quarterbacks, but Pelissero says it’ll take an injury-driven emergency for Rodgers to play again. At this point, no team is desperate enough to dance with the devil.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Rams OG Bill Murray ruptured his Achilles tendon in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Bill Murray

This is unfortunate. Murray, a backup, started at left guard and played well. He will now undergo surgery and begin rehab for the 2027 NFL season. The Rams’ offensive line is fairly banged up. Hopefully, the extra time off allows the unit to improve its health.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Brian Schottenheimer will remain the Cowboys’ head coach for the rest of the season.
item.description:
Brian Schottenheimer DAL Head Coach

Palmer’s report wasn’t entirely positive. He also believes that if the Cowboys’ performance does not improve, “there are going to be some decisions that Jerry Jones needs to make after the season.” It sounds like Schottenheimer may be coaching for his job for the rest of the year. Stay tuned.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report for Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock was limited again this week with tendinitis in his throwing arm’s elbow. With Sam Darnold (quad) back in action, Lock returns to his backup role.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: Evan Engram didn’t catch either of his two targets in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Evan Engram DEN Tight End

Engram was a complete non-factor, which is particularly disappointing after his six-catch, 74-yard effort in Week 11 against the Raiders. Unfortunately, this is much more inline with his previous production, and Engram can safely be ignored in Week 13 against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught his only target for one yard in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
Pat Freiermuth PIT Tight End

Freiermuth didn’t have his first target until the beginning of the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old was a consistent target of Aaron Rodgers, but he didn’t appear to have much of a rapport with Mason Rudolph in their first game together. Freiermuth can’t be trusted as more than a low-end TE2 for Week 13 against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-7 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant was able to make the most of an unfathomably bad day from Bo Nix, although it’s far from a fantasy stat line fantasy managers are clamoring for. Bryant has been one of the more consistent options for the Denver passing attack, but that’s not the compliment it should be. Bryant is at best a FLEX for Week 13 against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-8 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Courtland Sutton DEN Wide Receiver

To be fair to Sutton, Bo Nix was trying to get him the football. To be honest, he didn’t. Sutton was once among the better wideout options, but he’s been consistently putting up duds like this for too long in 2026 to count on him in fantasy. Even in a friendly matchup against the Dolphins in Week 13, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rico Dowdle rushed 11 times for 71 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos while catching one pass for three yards.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle was the much more effective runner between he and Jaylen Warren, although the bulk of the yardage came on one 27-yard scoot. He also lost a fumble, but the Steelers still gave him some carries after that turnover. A solid yardage day, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect similar production in Week 13 against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Michael Pittman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman was playing in his first game since Week 4, and he — and most of the Pittsburgh offense — didn’t have much chemistry with Mason Rudolph in a game where the Steelers’ defense was their best offense. The former Colt could be an option in the coming weeks, but shouldn’t be trusted in Week 13 against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jaylen Waddle caught 5-of-8 targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

It’s far from one of Waddle’s best games of his career, but when you consider how atrocious Bo Nix was Friday, it’s considerably more impressive. He wasn’t able to get deep down the field, but he was without hyperbole the only relatively effective offensive option for the Broncos in Week 12. He’s a WR4 for the upcoming match against his former employer in the Dolphins in Week 13.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 58 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
Germie Bernard PIT Wide Receiver

Bernard set up the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown with his long connection with Mason Rudolph. That was his only contribution, however, as Pittsburgh relied heavily on the run game as they built a big lead and didn’t appear to have a ton of trust in Rudolph in the rainy weather. Bernard doesn’t have much fantasy upside for the remainder of the year, and that includes his Week 13 showdown against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jaylen Warren rushed 20 times for 46 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren and Dowdle received all 31 rushing attempts as the Steelers relied heavily on the run game in Mason Rudolph’s first game as a starter. The 28-year-old tailback didn’t find much room, however, and this is back-to-back-to-back clunkers for Warren. He’ll try and get things going in Week 13 when Pittsburgh squares off against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jonah Coleman rushed 15 times for 26 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers while adding eight catches for 46 yards.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman was able to “save” his fantasy afternoon thanks to some checkdowns and screen passes, although outside of a 17-yard connection it was all for minimal yardage. The 23-year-old found zero room on the ground against the Steelers’ front seven, and plodding wouldn’t be an inaccurate description. Coleman has looked the part for most of the year and has a good chance to rebound in Week 13 against the lowly Dolphins, but this was ugly.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

After being ejected from Week 11, Metcalf was able to find the end zone in his first game with Mason Rudolph as he won a one-on-one battle with Pat Surtain II on a 22-yard score. I

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Bo Nix completed 22-of-40 passes for 169 yards with two interceptions in the Broncos’ 27-5, Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Bo Nix DEN Quarterback

Nix was atrocious in the first half and created two Pittsburgh touchdowns, one on a fumble returned for a score and one on an interception where it’s not clear who he was trying to throw the ball to. His third turnover was a desperation throw on 4th and forever in the middle of the final quarter. This was an ugly performance that showed Nix’s floor is among the lower of the quarterbacks fantasy managers would consider. He’ll be a QB2 for Week 13 in a matchup against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Mason Rudolph completed 9-of-15 passes for 142 yards with a touchdown in the Steelers’ 27-5, Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description:
Mason Rudolph PIT Quarterback

Rudolph’s first start since the trainwreck that was the Aaron Rodgers dismissal was uneven, but it was better than the production Rodgers was giving the Steelers over the past few weeks. He found DK Metcalf for a touchdown on a solid throw that allowed Metcalf to take advantage of his size, and he kept the chains moving in the first half, for the most part. The second half was far less impressive, but good enough, especially with Bo Nix playing atrocious football. Rudolph will still be hard to trust as a fantasy option for Week 13 against the Texans.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans sat out on Wednesday and practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday. We do not know today’s participation level, but he is clearly still rehabbing his Achilles tendinitis. Regardless, he is a high-end WR2 at worst whenever he is active. He will be catching passes thrown by capable backup Mac Jones against a tough Seahawks defense this week.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Mac Jones will start in Week 13 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Mac Jones SF Quarterback

Brock Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out, leaving Jones as the 49ers’ starter this week. Jones played very well in multiple starts last season, though he faces a tough Seahawks defense. Jones is a starter in two-quarterback leagues.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers ruled out Brock Purdy (ankle) for Week 12 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Mac Jones will start in Purdy’s stead. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Purdy is dealing with a mid-ankle sprain and that surgery is not necessary. The team is optimistic about his availability for Week 13 against the Giants. Jones piloted the offense efficiently last year and should be expected to do so again, albeit in a tough matchup this week.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: David Njoku (shoulder) is questionable for Week 12 against the Patriots.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku’s potential absence would allow Charlie Kolar, and theoretically Oronde Gadsden, to play more, but neither tight end qualifies as a top-12 option in that scenario. Justin Herbert (concussion) is also out.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Chargers ruled out Keaton Mitchell (knee) in Week 12 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Losing Mitchell helpfully condenses the Chargers’ backfield for fantasy purposes, though the offense will suffer with Justin Herbert (concussion) sidelined. Omarion Hampton is a volume-based RB2. Kimani Vidal is an RB3/4.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Chargers ruled out Justin Herbert (concussion) for Week 12 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Justin Herbert LAC Quarterback

Chargers backup QB DJ Uiagalelei is expected to start in Herbert’s stead. He threw a touchdown pass when Herbert left early due to a hand injury a few weeks back, but he is tough to rely on as anything more than a volatile QB2. Hopefully, Herbert can return for Week 13 against the Buccaneers.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks have managed Smith-Njigba’s reps in practice all year, and this week was no different. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but should be fine for Sunday. Smith-Njigba is an elite WR1, as always, and gets Sam Darnold (quad) back this week.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Sam Darnold (quad) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks’ starting quarterback will make his return for a divisional showdown against the 49ers. Darnold has been fairly banged up this year, but hopefully the time off was good for him. He is a QB2 in Week 12.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Jackson Powers-Johnson (Achilles) will not play in Las Vegas’ Week 12 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Jackson Powers-Johnson LV Offensive Lineman

The instant rule-out and talk of a potentially serious injury has us believing Powers-Johnson will hit IR ahead of Sunday Night Football. Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn have played in Powers-Johnson’s absence this year and one of them will likely start against the Browns.

item.title: Raheim Sanders (hip) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 12 game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Raheim Sanders CLE Running Back

Todd Monken said he’s “hoping” to activate Sanders, who has only gotten in limited practices this week. He sounds truly questionable for Sunday Night Football. If active, Sanders will cut into Dylan Sampson’s backup workload a bit.

Source: Zac Jackson

item.title: Browns signed LS Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.
item.description:
Rex Sunahara CLE Long Snapper

Sunahara, 30 years young, has been the Browns’ snapper of balls that go longer than the league average since 2024. He’s now inked through his age-34 season.

item.title: Abdul Carter (calf/illness) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Colts.
item.description:
Abdul Carter NYG Outside Linebacker

Carter is also no longer listed with an ankle injury, which is a good sign. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) is also cleared to face a Colts offense now led by Anthony Richardson.

Source: New York Giants

item.title: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 12 against the Colts.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely injured his groin last Friday and caught one pass for 35 yards two days later. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full today, which is encouraging. Likely is a TE1 for Week 12 against the Colts.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Carlton Davis (knee) won’t play in New England’s Week 12 game against the Chargers.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

He didn’t practice at all this week and doesn’t seem especially close to playing at this point. Davis has not played since Week 9. The Patriots are having enough trouble struggling with the maximum number of IR-return slots that Drake Maye hasn’t been placed on IR either, so we won’t slag them for Davis not being there, but he doesn’t look close.

item.title: Rams signed TE Jack Stoll off San Francisco’s practice squad.
item.description:
Jack Stoll

With both Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee week-to-week, the Rams have brought in reinforcements behind Colby Parkinson and Max Klare. There’s no need to project Stoll to real fantasy work, but he could find some playing time if they continue to play 13-personnel sets.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on Washington’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

A rough Cardinals defense could get Burks into the deep league conversation, but he’s had just six targets in two games since returning from the bye week. If he doesn’t do something this week, Brandon Aiyuk might be knocking on the door of his starting spot come Week 13.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on the Jaguars’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers will expectedly function as the Jaguars’ No. 1 wide receiver with Parker Washington (shoulder) sidelined and considered week-to-week. Meyers accordingly vaults into the WR2/3 range and could deliver a big stat line against a soft Titans defense.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Rashod Bateman (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

You know what you’re getting into if you start Bateman, but he did manage a touchdown grab against the Panthers last week and the Ravens have generally pumped up their passing usage since Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore. He’s probably a bit below the FLEX line in standard leagues, but it wouldn’t shock us if he landed in that area this week against the Texans.

item.title: Jaguars ruled out Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) for Week 12 against the Titans.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Chris Rodriguez should be added wherever he is available. Tuten will finally take a week off after playing through foot and ankle injuries for multiple weeks. He reportedly aggravated the issues in Week 11 against the Giants. Hopefully, Tuten will return for the Jaguars’ expectedly fantasy-friendly game against the Bears in Week 13.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Zay Flowers (ankle) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

He can be started as a low-end WR1 against a Texans outfit that has given up plenty of passing yards this year. Flowers has been a fixture on the injury report this year but hasn’t missed a game since Week 2.

item.title: Derrick Henry (concussion) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

He’ll get his normal workload, though he’s playing like more of a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 since the Jacoby Brissett takeover, against the Texans.

item.title: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Danielle Hunter HOU Defensive End

Hunter didn’t practice at any point this week. The hamstring injury has been described as short-term, but this is the third straight week he’ll miss with it. Perhaps he’ll have a chance to get back for Week 13.

item.title: Kayshon Boutte (hip) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Kayshon Boutte HOU Wide Receiver

Boutte did not practice at any point this week and has essentially become a boom-bust FLEX threat at best on a limited snap count. He is likely questionable for Week 13 and can be dropped in shallow leagues.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

With Kayshon Boutte out, it’s possible that Harrison could be Houston’s No. 3 wideout if they continue to manage things delicately with Tank Dell. He’ll be a tough FLEX play given his snap volume with the Texans even despite a nice matchup against the Ravens.

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Browns.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

We can’t know for sure, but it looks like the Raiders might choose to hold Bowers out through their Week 13 bye. He was limited on Wednesday, and although he was limited again on Thursday, he practiced with his injured ankle heavily taped. Today, he sat out. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak tends to let his players take the field on game day, even if they are at less than 100 percent, but Bowers must be viewed as truly questionable at best. If active, he should be in fantasy football lineups. In the meantime, make a backup plan.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Jalen McMillan (knee/calf) was limited in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

McMillan added the calf injury while trying to get off injured reserve with his knee, falling from a Thursday full session to a limited Friday. He’ll likely be questionable at best for Monday night.

item.title: Isaiah Williams (ribs) is not on New York’s final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams got in two full sessions to close out the week and should have a decent role against the Dolphins with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) sidelined. Still, we’d expect the Jets to try to ride their run game, so Williams isn’t a must-use FLEX play or anything like that.

item.title: Tee Higgins (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Saints.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins reportedly woke up with soreness in his hamstring today. He participated in the Bengals’ walkthrough, but left practice when team stretching began. He will be listed as a non-participant on the official injury report. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Higgins should be fine for Sunday’s game. Higgins has a long history of hamstring strains, particularly in his left leg, and the Bengals have occasionally used him as a decoy when hurt in the past. That said, he is a very talented player, capable of producing efficiently even if used minimally. Higgins should be in fantasy football lineups if active.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller now has back-to-back limited sessions. He has cobbled together four limited practices in a row and played through this injury last week. It’s possible he is held to 40 percent of the snaps again in Week 12 if we don’t see an upgrade on Friday, but with all three Panthers tight ends on the injury report, the whole situation will remain uncertain until Saturday. Mitchell Evans (Achilles) upgraded to a limited session after not practicing on Thursday, and Tommy Tremble (knee) also was limited for a second day in a row.

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) was limited in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

McMillan was not spotted on Thursday, so this is a good sign for his chances of suiting up on Monday Night Football against the Buccaneers. Still, there’s a non-zero chance he winds up with a questionable tag on Saturday.

item.title: Taliese Fuaga (knee) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

While Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, may or may not play, the team’s starting center, Erik McCoy (biceps), will make his return. Getting him back is good news for the Saints’ offense as a whole. Backup OT Asim Richards (knee) is also questionable.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Kyler Murray will back up Kirk Cousins in Week 12.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Murray was removed from the injury report on Friday and will be active for the first time since suffering his hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will likely be an inactive third quarterback.

Source: Ben Goessling

item.title: Noah Fant (calf) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Noah Fant NO Tight End

With Juwan Johnson (hamstring) sidelined, Fant had a chance to increase his role on Sunday. Getting hurt on Friday pretty much takes him off the TE2 radar. Jordyn Tyson could benefit as a go-to receiver in the short-to-intermediate area of the field.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Darrisaw MIN Tackle

At no point did he practice after leaving Week 11’s game in Mexico City with the shoulder injury. Ryan Van Demark replaced Darrisaw in mop-up duty and would seem likely to start this week.

item.title: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

It’s his third straight absence. Kevin O’Connell seemed optimistic that Addison would have more of a shot to play this week, but he remains practiceless since suffering the thumb injury in a Friday practice ahead of Week 10.

item.title: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 12 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Perhaps this will give Kellen Moore an excuse to actually get Jordyn Tyson on the field this week. Noah Fant should also benefit from Johnson’s absence, and has a non-zero chance of a TE1 fantasy day given the Bengals strong track record of letting tight ends run wild under DC Al Golden.

Source: Katherine Terrell

item.title: Ravens ruled out Vega Ioane (hand) for Week 12 against the Texans.
item.description:
Vega Ioane BAL Guard

The Ravens’ stud rookie right guard has had unfortunate injury luck thus far. He was already playing through knee and shoulder injuries when he injured his hand in yesterday’s practice. Perhaps the time off will help the other two issues heal. The Ravens also ruled out DT Nnamdi Madubuike and S Jaylinn Hawkins.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Woody Marks cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 12 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Woody Marks HOU Running Back

Marks will return for No. 2 running back duties after a one-game absence. With zero teams on bye, Marks makes for a shaky FLEX option. He was unable to produce reliably while operating as the team’s starter, and should mostly be viewed as a bench stash at this time.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Brandon Aiyuk will not be elevated from the practice squad for Washington’s Week 12 game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk WAS Wide Receiver

No surprise or shame there — Aiyuk literally just signed on Wednesday. We are curious to see if he’ll be able to get active for Week 13, when the Commanders have a tasty matchup against the Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans.

Source: John Keim

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) was not seen practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. ESPN’s Ryan McFadden noted yesterday that Bowers’ right ankle was “heavily wrapped up” yesterday, which wasn’t the case on Wednesday. Hopefully, today’s absence during the portion of practice open to the media is only a precautionary, rest-related move. We should know more when the official injury report drops later. Stay tuned.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Jake Ferguson has partial tears in his MCL and PCL.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

That explains why Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson would likely be out “multiple weeks” after injuring his knee in Week 9 against the Colts. We haven’t had an official update in a while, but the Cowboys are on bye in Week 14. Perhaps a Week 15 return is possible.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: Cole Holcomb (heel) will not play in the Steelers’ Week 12 game against the Broncos.
item.description:
Cole Holcomb PIT Linebacker

Holcomb was the only player listed as questionable entering the weekend, but the team has opted to sit him for this one after he suffered a heel injury in the previous week’s loss to the Eagles. In addition to Holcomb, the Steelers also declared WR Kaden Weten, QB Drew Allar, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, LB Alex Highsmith, and DT Gabe Rubio inactive for this week. Will Howard will serve as the backup for starting QB Mason Rudolph.

Source: Nick Farbaugh

item.title: 49ers ruled out Brock Purdy (ankle) for Week 12 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Mac Jones will start in Purdy’s stead. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Purdy is dealing with a mid-ankle sprain, and the team is optimistic about his availability for Week 13 against the Giants. Jones piloted the offense efficiently last year and should be expected to do so again, albeit in a tough matchup this week.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey S Taylor Rapp, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley inactive for Week 12 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Sam Ehlinger DEN Quarterback

The Broncos will be operating at close to full strength against the Steelers in a game that could feature some inclement weather and low temperatures. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman could be in line for a busy day, with J.K. Dobbins suspended by the team for this week. Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in last week’s win over the Raiders.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

Branch has now been sidelined each of the last four weeks, missing Week 9 and 10 before their Week 11 bye, and did not practice at any point this week. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve” list for players who weren’t close to playing.

item.title: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jahan Dotson ATL Wide Receiver

Olmaide Zachcheaus will be Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver behind Drake London, and after that it turns to Chris Blair and Beaux Collins with Zachariah Branch also hurt. This will likely be a situation that forces the Falcons to condense the target tree and throw at their main three of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts.

item.title: Denzel Boston (quad) is questionable for the Browns’ Week 12 game against the Raiders.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

According to Cabot, Boston was a DNP all week but still managed to draw the questionable tag. Given his week’s worth of DNPs, it’s hard to imagine the rookie suiting up on Sunday night, but it sounds like the Browns will give him some additional time to try and heal up before ruling him out. Fantasy managers planning to hold out until a decision is made would be wise to stash Jerry Jeudy or another player from Sunday or Monday night’s games as a pivot off Boston in the event he is ruled out.

Source: Mary kay Cabot

item.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said he “wouldn’t anticipate” Romeo Doubs (shoulder) being ready for action yet.
item.description:
Romeo Doubs NE Wide Receiver

Doubs was ruled out when official designations come out. Most players on IR will get a questionable tag on their chances to return regardless of the surrounding data, so it’s not a great sign that Doubs couldn’t even muster that. He remains week-to-week and has little fantasy relevancy unless Drake Maye can muster a comeback.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Carson Beck (back) will not play in Week 12 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck will miss a second straight game with his back injury after missing all of practice this week. The rookie QB has dealt with back issues for the majority of the year, but will now set his sights on returning in Week 13 against the Eagles. That said, the Cardinals have a Week 14 bye, which could give them a reason to sideline Beck for at least one more week and let him heal up before returning for the final four games of the regular season.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals in Week 12 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Josh Johnson ARI Quarterback

Johnson will get the start on Sunday against the Commanders in what will be a “revenge” game for the 40-year-old vet. Although, in fairness to Johnson, a lot of games are revenge games for the well-traveled vet. Things didn’t fare too well for Johnson in his first start of the season against the Chiefs, as he threw for 155 yards and one touchdown on the road, but did a good job of limiting turnovers. He’s nothing more than a QB3/desperation play in 2QB and superflex leagues.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
item.description:
Tyler Higbee

ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are expected to serve as the top two tight ends in Sean McVay’s 12-heavy personnel, but the team could look to add a free agent tight end or two in the days ahead.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Rams TE Davis Allen is considered week-to-week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
item.description:
Davis Allen

NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the news. Allen will reportedly go to the Rams’ facilities today for a full evaluation to determine the approximate length of his absence, but with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Tyler Higbee (chest) also considered week-to-week, the Rams are suddenly very thin at tight end. Rookie second-rounder Max Klare and veteran Colby Parkinson are the only healthy tight ends currently on the roster, but it’s possible the Rams will look to add one or two more free agents to fill their needs at the position. It’s hard to imagine either Parkinson or Klare seeing enough of a role in the Rams’ passing game to become fantasy-viable players in the weeks ahead.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) will not play in Week 12 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

With a Week 13 bye on tap for the Jets, the team is hoping two extra weeks of rest will be more than enough for Cooper to play in Week 14 against the Broncos. Cooper has not played since re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Bills and has now missed six of a possible 12 games in his rookie season. It’s possible this is the last update we receive on Cooper until the Jets return from their bye week, but fantasy managers in need of help over the next two weeks can safely drop him where needed.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Parker Washington

According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away.

Source: John Shipley

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. Goedert has caught 33 passes for 355 yards and two touchdowns this season, with both of his scores coming in Week 1against the Commanders. Zach Ertz’s 39 offensive snaps and 19 routes run both led the Eagles’ tight end room on the day, and could point to him operating as Philly’s TE1 if Goedert were to miss any time.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. Rice will get one final week in the WR2 ranks when the Chiefs take on the Rams next week. Another quiet performance will send him tumbling down the rankings.

item.title: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-7 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce was the only member of the Chiefs’ passing attack to find any success in this game. Being battered by the elements, Patrick Mahomes relied on his trusted tight end for a handful of big plays throughout the contest. One of them was a 21-yard toss to the nine-yard line at the end of the first half that set up a short field goal. Kelce, however, paid the price with a helmet to the back that left him on the ground in pain for a while. He ultimately played through the issue, though we expect to see him on the injury report next week. Kelce, unfortunately, did not go out on a high note, dropping a long pass that would have at least pushed the game into overtime. With a potential shootout on tap versus the Rams, Kelce will remain inside the top 12 fantasy tight ends next week.

item.title: Ty Johnson caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

Johnson spiked for 55 yards on seven catches last week. That usage was nowhere to be found on Thanksgiving. It was a rain-soaked rock-fight of a game in which the Bills barely even tried to pass. Josh Allen threw the ball 21 times and only 10 were caught. The low volume axed any chance Johnson had of an encore. Facing a lowly Patriots team in Week 13, we don’t expect much work for Buffalo’s third-down back next week. Johnson will be buried in the RB5 ranks.

item.title: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Shakir led the Bills in targets, catches, and yards, but it was a memorable Thanksgiving for the worst kind of reason. Josh Allen tossed him a simple screen pass in the red zone late in the third quarter, but Shakir failed to corral the ball and bobbled it right into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. The good news for Shakir is that the blunder didn’t land him in the doghouse. Allen’s very next attempt went to Shakir for a six-yard gain. Shakir has been a steady option out of the slot this year, but the spike weeks have been nonexistent. He has one touchdown and a single 100-yard game through 11 appearances. He will be stuck in the WR4 ranks when the Bills take on the Patriots next week.

item.title: Josh Downs caught 1-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Josh Downs KC Wide Receiver

This was by far Downs’ quietest game as a Chief, though his second half special teams play was rather loud. Downs made a pair of questionable decisions on fourth quarter punts, twice fielding the ball near the Chiefs’ own goal line. Neither gamble came close to working. The only good news was Downs did not cough the ball up. Downs’ snaps once again didn’t really kick up on offense, as he was on the field for just 16 plays. Perhaps that will finally, finally change in Week 13 against the Rams. For now, Downs is a boom/bust WR3 in fantasy football.

item.title: Xavier Worthy was held without a catch on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

It was a rainy, wind-swept night in Buffalo, but Patrick Mahomes still managed to have a decent evening. The same was not true for his former No. 2 receiver, who “zero balled” even as also-rans like Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals caught passes. Held to just two catches in three games since Josh Downs’ Kansas City arrival, Worthy is turning into a tough hold even in 14-team leagues.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Two catches looks bad until you realize Josh Allen completed only 10 throws in a rain-marred affair. It’s still sadly unsurprising Kincaid was one of the biggest victims of a run-heavy game environment. Rather amazingly, tonight was the fifth time in 10 2026 appearances Kincaid was held to three-or-fewer targets. He’s becoming more of a fringe TE1 than locked-in option, though the return of byes for Week 13 means he will probably still crack the top 12 against the Patriots.

item.title: Emmett Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills, adding four catches for 24 yards.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

Johnson made his third start in place of an injured Kenneth Walker this week. While the Bills did a far better job of bottling up the rookie than either of Johnson’s previous opponents, they still couldn’t shut him down entirely. After a quiet first half, Johnson punched in a goal line touchdown on the Chiefs’ opening drive of the third quarter. Johnson still managed 96 yards from scrimmage and what will almost certainly be another RB1 weekly finish, even with the Chiefs’ offense amounting to little in a torrential downpour. Walker practiced this week, but the Chiefs didn’t want to rush him back for a short turnaround to Thanksgiving. He now has seven days to get ready for the Chiefs’ Week 13 game against the Rams. We suspect he’ll be active, which will relegate Johnson to a change-of-pace role. Fantasy managers, however, won’t want to cut one of the league’s most valuable backups loose, even if his role is set to decline.

item.title: James Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
item.description:
James Cook BUF Running Back

Sportsbooks correctly cratered the total of this game throughout the week to account for gusting winds, pouring rain, and a chilly temperature. Joe Brady’s response to these miserable conditions was to feed his top back for all four quarters. Cook set a season-high in carries and scored his 10th straight rushing touchdown. Buffalo’s lead back didn’t score in Week 1 and has found the end zone in every subsequent game. Cook will be a good bet to find the end zone at least once when he takes on the downtrodden Patriots next week. Per usual, Cook will be a top-five fantasy option.

item.title: DJ Moore caught 2-of-6 targets for 15 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

On a rain-drenched, run-heavy night in Buffalo, Josh Allen completed only 10 passes. Translation, there wasn’t a whole lot for Moore to do even as he tied for the team lead in looks. That being said, volume has not been Moore’s strong suit this season, as he’s averaging just six targets. Although that number is skewed a bit by an injury-shortened Week 2, Moore hasn’t quite had the alpha role fantasy managers had in mind. He is still pacing as a solid option on the WR2/3 borderline, one whose best football could arguably still be ahead of him. The Patriots could go either way as a Week 13 road matchup.

item.title: Josh Allen completed 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 13-10, Week 12 win over the Chiefs, adding seven carries for 43 yards.
item.description:
Josh Allen BUF Quarterback

Playing in a cold downpour in Buffalo, it was a sloppy mess of a game for Allen, who posted his worst passing line of the year by every metric. The two interceptions, however, can’t be put entirely on him. The first was a tipped pass in the red zone that fell into the hands of a Chiefs defensive back. The second was a screen to Khalil Shakir, which was bobbled directly into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. Even if you toss out the interceptions as bad luck, Week 12 was still the lowlight of his season and then some. The last time Allen completed fewer than half of his passes was Week 5 of the 2024 season. He averaged fewer than four yards per attempt for the first time since 2019. For fantasy purposes, Allen’s issues were compounded by a lack of volume, which has been a recurring theme for the Buffalo offense this year. While we aren’t expecting the team to air it out versus the struggling Patriots next week, Allen should at least be far more efficient in Week 13. He remains the QB1 overall with ease despite the Thanksgiving bust.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards in the Chiefs’ 13-10, Week 12 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Neither Mahomes nor Josh Allen was able to get much going in what was supposed to be the game of the season. With rain drenching the field and pelting players, there was simply no way for either team to consistently string together successful passes. The Chiefs also committed several special teams blunders, including but not limited to a botched snap and subsequent shank by punter Matt Araiza, a tipped punt, and yet another missed field goal by Harrison Butker. Not to be outdone, Mahomes bungled multiple snaps of his own. The elements and Buffalo’s resurgent defense combined to shut down Mahomes, who entered the week riding a two-game molten hot streak. The best he could do was avoid negative plays and live to fight another day. Mahomes was sacked just once and did not turn the ball over, though he had a close call in the fourth quarter with a throw-away gone awry. This game and its ugly conditions will ultimately go down as a write-off for fantasy managers who started either quarterback. Mahomes will get a QB1 redo in a week when he takes on the Rams.

item.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is still confident in head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
item.description:
Brian Schottenheimer DAL Head Coach

Jones said he is not considering a head coaching change. This came just minutes after the Cowboys’ catastrophic meltdown against the Eagles on Thanksgiving. Dallas gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter and lost on a last-second field goal. Schottenheimer stripped DC Christian Parker of play-calling duties two weeks ago. The Cowboys gave up 79 points to Cam Ward and Joe Milton in senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine’s first two games calling plays on defense. Schottenheimer has had no issues getting points on the board, but his Cowboys have routinely found spectacular ways to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. He is now 12-16-1 as the team’s head coach. He will need to turn things around in the final quarter of this season if he wants to keep his job beyond 2026.

Source: Jon Machota

item.title: Elijah Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Elijah Moore PHI Wide Receiver

Elijah Moore catching passes from Joe Milton makes a lot of sense on August 19, but is a little more surprising on Thanksgiving. Still, the 26-year-old was able to put together a solid day and helped set up the game-winning field goal with a couple of catches on the final drive. It’s hard to imagine Moore is fantasy relevant in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but he and Milton did appear to be on the same page.

item.title: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-6 targets for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Makai Lemon PHI Wide Receiver

Lemon was vastly improved from his disappointing one-catch against the Steelers the previous week. He brought in his first touchdown since Week 7 — also against the Cowboys — and it got the Eagles to within two points with just over two minutes left. The Eagles weren’t able to convert the two-point conversion, but still came up with the improbable victory. Lemon will try and build on this effort against the Cardinals in Week 13.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Will Shipley rushed 10 times for 46 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley took over after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, and while the Eagles were mostly in pass-mode because they fall behind 31-0, Shipley did a decent job in his limited touches. If Barkley can’t go in Week 13 against the Cardinals, Shipley is an interesting fill-in for that contest.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: KaVontae Turpin caught 1-of-3 targets for a 31-yard touchdown while adding a 10-yard rush in the Cowboys’ Week 12 win over the Eagles.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

Turpin did most of the work on a dump-off from Dak Prescott. The 30-year-old remains an impact player on special teams, but despite the score, he offers very little fantasy upside for the remainder of the season. Or next season.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: George Pickens caught five-of-nine targets for 67 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens dropped what would have likely been a touchdown from Dak Prescott early in the game. He also had a catch that would have resulted in a first down, but after being hit hard, he went nine yards backwards and wasn’t given forward progress. After impressing the previous two weeks, this was a disappointing effort. He’ll get a chance to rebound in Week 13 against the Seahawks in a Monday Night Football showdown.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 134 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
CeeDee Lamb DAL Wide Receiver

Lamb also committed two pass interference penalties; one that wiped a touchdown off the board, although the Cowboys would end up scoring a few plays later. The 27-year-old was still able to fantasy day while going over 100 yards for the sixth time in the 2026 season. Lamb will remain a WR1 even with a tough matchup coming in Week 13 against the Seahawks.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: DeVonta Smith caught 11-of-14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith was able to bring down an impressive 50-yard touchdown throw from Joe Milton to get the Eagles within two scores. He did the same on a 45-yarder a quarter later in what was easily his best game of the 2026 season. The hamstring issue that has limited Smith as of late did not appear to be an issue Thursday, and he appeared to have some quality chemistry with Milton. Smith is a WR2 on paper for a showdown in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but this effort shows the WR1 upside is palpable.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Javonte Williams rushed 28 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles while adding three receptions for 22 yards and a receiving score.
item.description:
Javonte Williams DAL Running Back

Williams ran in for two scores in the first half, and then was able to just get into the end zone on a connection with Dak Prescott for his third score of the first half. The second-half was quiet for the tailback, but the damage was done while reaching 15 total scores on the season. Williams will be in the RB1 conversation, even with the sledding likely significantly tougher against the Seahawks in Week 13.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Joe Milton completed 21of-31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Eagles’ 39-38, Week 12 win over the Cowboys while adding 15 yards and a touchdown on the ground.
item.description:
Joe Milton PHI Quarterback

Milton certainly isn’t boring. He even showed off some impressive touch at times, but the most impressive throw was a bomb that went 58 yards in the air for a score to DaVonta Smith. He nearly matched that dart with another 45-yarder to Smith in the third quarter as he lived up to the Bazooka Joe nickname. He even showed off some scrambling ability, particularly on a 15-yard scrambling into the end zone in the middle of the fourth quarter. The only real mistake was a forced throw with the Eagles down eight on the next possession, but he followed that up with a brilliant 24-yard throwing score to Makai Lemon. He made enough plays on the final drive to get the Eagles into field-goal range, and complete a three-touchdown comeback win. It was a vastly improved effort for Milton over the Week 11 contest versus the Steelers, albeit it against a significantly worse defense. Milton will likely get the start in Week 13 against the Cardinals, and offers a wide range of potential fantasy outcomes.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-27 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 38-36, Week 12 win over the Eagles, adding 19 yards on the ground with a rushing score.
item.description:
Dak Prescott DAL Quarterback

The NFC East is something, folks. Prescott had a big day even with a couple of long runs overturned due to penalty, and some “hidden yardage” due to pass interference that put the Cowboys into scoring position. He fired a pair of touchdowns to running backs in the first half and helped Dallas build a 28-10 lead going into the half. The Cowboys would blow that lead in spectacular fashion, and Prescott took a horrific sack to set up good field position before the game-winning field goal for Philadelphia. He will try and keep the good statistical run going in Week 13 against the Seahawks in a Monday Night Football matchup.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker, QB Garrett Nussmeier, CB Melvin Smith, DT Omarr Norman-Lott, T Diego Pounds, OL Jaylon Moore and DT Marcus Harris inactive for Week 13 against the Bills.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Walker will miss at least one more game while dealing with his groin strain, meaning Emmett Johnson should be the workhorse against the Buffalo defense. Nussmeier will be the emergency third quarterback.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is active for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

As expected, Kincaid will play after getting in a couple of limited practices ahead of the Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs. He should be treated as a lower-end TE1 for the contest. The Bills inactives versus Kansas City will be CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, OLB Mike Danna, OT Jude Bowry and DL Greg Gaines.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding five receptions for 47 yards.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

Gibbs is the most valuable player in fantasy football, regardless of format. Since scoring twice from one yard out isn’t enough for him, Gibbs ripped off a clean 70-yard touchdown run on the Lions’ ninth drive — and that probably wasn’t his most impressive play. One drive earlier, Gibbs took a run to the right side, and multiple Bears defenders broke past the offensive line. One got a hand on him, but he changed direction and took off for a 32-yard gain down the sideline. The impending 2026 league-winner should be treated as the overall RB1 in Week 13 against the Falcons’ beatable run defense.

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 44 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

The Lions’ No. 1 tight end generated multiple double-digit gains today, including an 11-yard touchdown on a hitch-and-go just before halftime. He played through his ankle injury without issue after beginning the week limited in practice, notably diving to make a 17-yard catch. LaPorta is a TE1 against the Falcons next week.

item.title: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-9 targets for 68 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding one rush for 12 yards.
item.description:
Jameson Williams DET Wide Receiver

The Lions got Williams involved on crossers, corners and screen passes today, but a few missed connections proved costly. Jared Goff targeted Williams in the end zone on the opening drive, but the pass fell incomplete. On the Lions’ fifth drive, Williams got behind the defense, but stumbled slightly, resulting in an overthrow instead of a long score. On the Lions’ 10th drive, Williams was unable to secure a third-down target at the Bears’ 25-yard line and accidentally tipped the pass to a Bears safety instead. That said, Williams deserves credit for generating a 39-yard gain on a corner route that helped set up Sam LaPorta’s touchdown just before halftime. Williams remains a volatile WR2 in Week 13 against the Jaguars.

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-10 targets for 146 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown shot out of the gates in this one, generating two explosive plays on the Lions’ opening drive. He needed a breather after being sandwiched between two Bears defenders on a deep completion on the Lions’ third drive. He played through a ribs issue a couple of weeks ago, and may reappear on the injury report with the same issue next week. Despite the hard hit, St. Brown stayed hot and continued ripping off long gains. A Bears defensive back committed pass interference against him on a target thrown to St. Brown right at the goal line. The ball fell incomplete, but the penalty setup one of Jahmyr Gibbs’ rushing touchdowns. St. Brown remains an elite WR1 against the Falcons in Week 13.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert suffered a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game and was ruled out a quarter later. The 31-year-old will get a week-plus to get healthy for Week 13 against the Cardinals, but for now Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt will be the uninspiring tight end options.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Jared Goff completed 25-of-36 passes for 313 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Lions’ 35-39, Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
item.description:
Jared Goff DET Quarterback

Goff’s first career Thanksgiving interception was not his fault. Jameson Williams tipped the pass right into Bears S Dillon Thieneman’s hands. Goff played very well on the day, and looked unstoppable whenever he targeted Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff nearly tacked on a second passing touchdown on a trick-play pass to OL Larry Borom in the end zone, but the pass unfortunately fell incomplete. Goff remains a locked-in QB1 next week against the Falcons.

item.title: Salvon Ahmed rushed three times for 50 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding two receptions for 17 yards.
item.description:
Salvon Ahmed CHI Running Back

Ahmed provided the Bears with needed sparks on more than one occasion today, using his speed to initially rip off a 46-yard run on the Bears’ third drive. He later made a slick diving catch for a first down on the Bears’ 10th drive. He can be picked up in 14-team leagues at this time, though he is only a bench stash.

item.title: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 15 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding one reception for 14 yards.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai ran inefficiently this week, but that did not stop him from bullying his way into the end zone for a pair of short touchdowns. The burly back may still be rounding into form after his lengthy turf toe-related absence, but he remains a featured player in the Bears’ elite offense. Monangai is an RB2/FLEX against the Jaguars next week.

item.title: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 65 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding seven receptions for 97 yards.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift was extremely efficient on his touches against the Lions, which was good because the Bears got Kyle Monangai and Salvon Ahmed going in this one as well. Swift had two 30-plus-yard gains today. His first was a catch in the flats, which he took down the right sideline after juking two Lions defenders. The second was a clean touchdown run in which he faked right before cutting back to the left and outrunning the defense. He regularly operated as a needed checkdown option for Caleb Williams today. Swift is a borderline RB1/2 against the Jaguars next week.

item.title: Caleb WIlliams told reporters that he was “fine” after undergoing X-rays following the Week 12 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

Williams said that he thought there was just a bruise on his abdomen after taking a fall. The signal-caller will get a mini-bye before the Bears take on the Jaguars in Week 13, and should be good to go for that contest.

Source: Jason Lieser

item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

That’s back-to-back missed practices for Boston. The 22-year-old still could be a go for Week 12 against the Raiders, but he’ll need to get in at least a limited session, and he doesn’t provide a ton of fantasy upside even if he does play for that matchup.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

Burden’s impact on the game was bigger than it was in the box score. He went in motion and helped block on the interior for Kyle Monangai’s first rushing touchdown. Aside from that, Burden generated a 25-yard gain on a slick post route and a 15-yard gain that helped set up Rome Odunze’s 41-yard score. Burden nearly hauled in a 46-yard pass on the Bears’ eighth drive, but Caleb Williams overthrew him. Burden was also flagged for offensive pass interference for what should have been considered justifiable handfighting. Burden took an end around for just one yard. Lions S Kerby Joseph delivered a helmet-to-helmet hit on the play, but was not flagged for it. Burden will be a WR2 against the Jaguars in Week 13.

item.title: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 39-35, Week 12 win over the Lions, adding three rushes for 15 yards.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

The Bears trailed 24-35 when they got the ball back with a little over eight minutes remaining in the game. Williams then activated “Iceman” mode, linking up with Luther Burden and Rome Odunze (twice) for 71 yards, one passing touchdown and a successful QB keeper on the two-point conversion. A Lions interception and consecutive turnovers on downs for both teams resulted in the Bears getting the ball back with just over two minutes remaining in the game. Aided by a 15-yard facemask penalty on the Lions, Williams again led the offense down the field before firing a perfectly placed ball to Rome Odunze in the back-right corner of the end zone for a six-yard score, powering the Bears to a 39-35 fourth-quarter comeback. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs reports that although Williams participated in all post-game celebration activities, he was taken for an X-ray afterward. We await an update. Stay tuned.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: Speaking with the Pittsburgh-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac, Steelers president Art Rooney II said Aaron Rodgers was not a “good teammate” following his release.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers

In a story published by Dulac on Thursday, Rooney said the Steelers are “100 percent” committed to head coach Mike McCarthy, while adding that “insubordination will not be tolerated” as far as Rodgers is concerned. According to Dulac, Rodgers and McCarthy met on Tuesday night, just hours before the QB’s benching, and presented McCarthy with an ultimatum: “let me call the plays or just release me.” What followed from there was Rodgers’ benching and eventual release after he went scorched earth on the Steelers and McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers will be free to sign with any team when he inevitably clears waivers later in the day, but for now, no potential suitor has emerged for the soon-to-be retired QB, who has been among the least efficient in the league over the last few seasons.

Source: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

item.title: Colby Parkinson caught both targets for minus one yard in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. The Rams have some things to figure out given the sheer number of bodies missing after also losing two offensive linemen in the game. The long week hopefully affords them enough time to return to health ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Chiefs.

item.title: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Konata Mumpfield

Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. Mumpfield remains the player with the most weekly upside for as long as Davante Adams remains sidelined, of available pass catchers, a unit that took two more hits with the departures of tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen. Fantasy managers are likely better off leaving Mumpfield on the waiver wire or on their bench.

item.title: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. Given the nature of the injury, this could be the new norm for a Rams team that continues to push for a postseason bid following a 2-4 start to their 2026 season, leaving Williams a touchdown-driven RB3 for the time being.

item.title: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Blake Corum

The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. The backfield split between Corum and Kyren Williams has taken a stark turn of late, with Corum now the preferred option on early downs and Kyren the preferred change of pace and clear passing situation back, a split that now leaves Corum the favorite for weekly production. He will remain an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 13 matchup against the Chiefs.

item.title: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Matthew Stafford

The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half. In total, the Rams attempted more runs than the Packers ran offensive plays (47 to 44), with this game marking the first game in the Sean McVay era in which a single back carried the football 30 or more times. It also marked the second consecutive game in which the Rams gained more than 200 yards on the ground, leaving Stafford with little volume as the reigning MVP failed to return a usable fantasy score for the fifth time this season while also failing to pass for a touchdown for the third time this season. The Rams saw two tight ends depart with injury as both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen were unable to finish the game, potentially something to keep an eye on as the Rams prepare to face the Chiefs in Week 13, particularly in the absence of both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Stafford remains an upside QB2 in fantasy circles.

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft continues to look miles behind where he was during his breakout 2025 season before suffering a torn ACL, lacking burst out of routes while struggling through mental mistakes. Another such mistake appeared against the Rams when Kraft was stripped of the football in the first quarter following his longest reception in the game. The once-imposing Green Bay offense feel completely flat following the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion, failing to score after the break while running just 44 total offensive plays. The Packers look to lick their wounds following back-to-back losses ahead of a Week 13 road meeting with the Saints, where Kraft will remain a frustrating TE2.

item.title: Matthew Golden caught 1-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden found himself in lockdown coverage throughout, particularly following the departure of fellow receiver Christian Watson in the second quarter. The talented second-year receiver has seen double-digit targets in six of 11 games in his sophomore campaign and could be headed for another high-target game against the Saints in Week 13, pending Watson’s availability on a long week. Golden would be a legitimate WR1, should Watson miss, and an upside WR2, should Watson play.

Lead back Josh Jacobs appeared close to suiting up coming out of their bye and could make his way back into the starting lineup on a long week ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Saints.

item.title: Jordan Love completed 17-of-29 passes for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Packers’ 26-13, Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding seven yards on one carry.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

it was the second consecutive game with three turnovers for the Packers as two second half interceptions thrown by Love were a microcosm of the team’s inability to hang with the Rams without their top option through the air. Christian Watson departed in the second quarter with a concussion after being knocked out on a vicious hit down the sideline, leaving the Packers in a hole they could not climb out of despite taking a tied game into the break. It is possible for Watson to clear concussion protocol in a long week of preparation, but Love could realistically be without his top option when the Packers travel to New Orleans to face the Saints in Week 13. In desperate need of a win following back-to-back losses to current playoff teams, the Packers head into the final two months of the regular season on the outside looking in at the NFC playoff picture.

item.title: Christian Watson (head) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 12 against the Rams.

Watson briefly departed the game after catching a pass on the first play from scrimmage, initially deemed questionable to return with a thigh injury. Watson was then the target of a vicious hit down the sideline for which Kamren Kinchens was ejected from the game. He remained down on the field before walking to the locker room under hit own power. Watson caught all four targets for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to departing. Although no update has been passed from the team, it appears as if Watson will enter the league’s concussion protocol after appearing to be knocked out, making him worse than questionable to return.

Daiyan Henley LAC Linebacker

Henley missed Week 11 with a knee injury and continues to sit for the Chargers’ walk-through practice to open the week. Also missing the walk-through were DT Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), CB Tarheeb Still (ankle), EDGE Akheem Mesidor (ankle), S Kendall Williamson (calf), and DB Deane Leonard (groin). It’s hard to believe this many Chargers defenders will sit this week but the team released a practice report with 14 DNPs on Wednesday. We can expect a few of these players to return to practice later this week and play in Week 12 against the Patriots.

item.title: David Njoku (shoulder) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Playing in his just his second game off I.R., Njoku suffered the upper-body injury against the Jets last Sunday. We already had practically nonexistent expectations for Njoku becoming TE2 relevant, but the new issue coupled with DJ Uiagalelei’s likely Week 12 start has him further from 12-team league lineups than ever.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell was listed as a DNP for the Chargers’ Wednesday walk-through. He suffered the knee injury in the first half of the team’s Week 11 loss to the Jets, only playing on a kick return afterwards and exiting the game in the second half. Mitchell does not need to be in fantasy lineups, though a potential absence would further boost Omarion Hampton’s resurgence for Week 12 against the Patriots.

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) and Abraham Lucas (ankle) are out for Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson SEA Guard

Neither Nelson or Lucas practiced on Wednesday and Macdonald declared both offensive lineman out this week against the 49ers. The Seahawks will dig into their offensive line depth to deal with the 49ers pass rush this week.

item.title: Drew Lock (right elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock continues to deal with an elbow injury, getting in a limited session on Wednesday. Sam Darnold was practicing in full and already announced to start in Week 12, so Lock can go back to fantasy benches and be cut for other waiver wire adds or stashes.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba SEA Wide Receiver

Smith-Njigba was listed on the practice report with an ankle issue earlier this season, but has not missed a game. This is likely just load management for the 24-year-old receiver. Expect Smith-Njigba to still play in Week 12 against the 49ers.

item.title: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Danielle Hunter HOU Defensive End

Hunter is dealing with a hamstring strain, missing the past two games for the Texans. He starts out this week not practicing and will need to practice in some capacity to have a shot at returning in Week 12 against the Ravens.

item.title: Kayshon Boutte (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Kayshon Boutte HOU Wide Receiver

Boutte popped up on the injury report with a hip issue and did not practice Wednesday. With Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) potentially returning this week, Boutte does not need to be on the fantasy radar for Week 12 against the Ravens.

item.title: Rashod Bateman (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman was hobbled after taking a hard hit in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. He pops up on the injury report with a groin issue to start the week, though he was still limited in practice. Bateman is hardly fantasy relevant at this point, but an absence would indicate more Ja’Kobi Lane targets for Week 12 against the Texans.

item.title: Zay Flowers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers dealt with ankle issues earlier this season and now pops up on the injury report with a limited designation due to the ankle. He is still trending to play in Week 12, where he will operate as the Ravens’ WR1 for Jacoby Brissett against the Texans. Barring setbacks, the ankle should not limit Flowers too much as he sits in the fantasy WR2 rankings this week.
