item.title: Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, DE Larrell Murchison, OLB Darryl Peterson III, C Coleman Shelton, G Steve Avila, and OLB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 12 against the Packers.
item.description:
Ty Simpson

Simpson will operate as the team’s emergency third quarterback. Avila and Shelton were declared out heading into the day, leaving the Rams offensive line short-handed against a Packers defensive line getting Micah Parsons back.

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee) is active for Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons is officially back after the Packers activated him off the PUP list this week. He is back nearly a year after suffering a torn ACL last season, making his debut on Thanksgiving eve against the Rams. The Packers pass rush gets a boost with the return of the five-time Pro Bowler this week.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs was limited in the Packers’ practices this week, but is not ready to return to play just yet. Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd will split the backfield opportunities in his absence. The Packers also declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and OL Mekhi Becton inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.

item.title: NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reports Kyren Williams “has been battling turf toe for the past month.”
item.description:
Kyren Williams

Williams was on the Rams’ injury report this week with a toe injury before getting cleared off the report before Wednesday. Pelissero reveals that Williams told him he has been battling turf toe for the past month. This stretch coincides with Blake Corum’s increased opportunities while Williams has seen his role reduced to more of a backfield split. Williams will continue to play through the injury, but expect Corum to still be heavily involved as a result.

Source: Netflix

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is questionable for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid was limited in practice all week but said he would most likely play. The Bills also listed Christian Benford (groin), T.J. Sanders (shoulder), O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle), and Dorian Williams (calf) as limited for Thursday night after a week of limited practices for each player.

item.title: Kyler Murray (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Murray was listed as a limited participant for the Vikings’ walk-through practice. Since going down with a hamstring injury, Murray’s starting role has been taken over by Kirk Cousins. Even if Murray is good to go for Week 12, he is likely to be in the backup role to Cousins against the Falcons.

item.title: Tai Felton (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
item.description:
Tai Felton MIN Wide Receiver

Felton pops up on the injury report with a limited listing as he deals with a hip injury. The second-year wide receiver saw a team-high 12 targets in Week 11 against the 49ers and has seen increased opportunities with Jordan Addison still dealing with a thumb injury. Also limited was Myles Price (knee/groin). Both Price and Felton offer limited deep-league upside with Addison out. Felton is the receiver to roster, if you must.

item.title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Christian Darrisaw MIN Tackle

Darrisaw seemingly re-injured his shoulder in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Minnesota just held a walk-through, but the franchise left tackle starts out not practicing. He is truly questionable ahead of Week 12 against the Falcons.

item.title: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

Addison has yet to practice since undergoing thumb surgery last week. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Monday that the 24-year-old may not “necessarily” be back in Week 12 against the Falcons. Tai Felton will continue to get increased reps with Addison out.

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

White dealt with this issue last week, but managed to be active on Monday night. He should be fine for backup duties in Week 1 2 against the Cardinals, though Jacory Croskey-Merritt is likely the only fantasy starter in this backfield.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks continues to play through his foot injury, albeit mostly ineffectively. He is a boom-bust downfield wide receiver who faces a tremendously soft Cardinals pass defense this week. Burks does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Jayden Daniels (left elbow/left hand) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Daniels’ left elbow issue is obviously not new, but the left hand injury is. That said, he is practicing in full and gets an exceptionally soft matchup against the Cardinals’ defense this week. Daniels is a high-end QB1, as usual.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Denzel Boston (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston continues to rack up lower-body injuries, though he tends to play through them. He dealt with a toe injury last week, catching just one pass for 16 yards. His practice participation is worth tracking closely this week.

Source: Paul H. Gutierrez

item.title: Michael Mayer (back) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Browns.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

Mayer injured his back in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he is evidently good to go this week. Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited today, tentatively putting him on track to face the Browns this weekend.

Source: Paul H. Gutierrez

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers closed last week with two limited sessions, listed with ankle and quad injuries. Fortunately, the quad injury is no longer an issue. He is tentatively on track to play in Week 12 against the Browns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic that Bowers will play this weekend, adding that having a bye in Week 13 will not factor into whether Bowers suits up this week.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jahan Dotson ATL Wide Receiver

Dotson and Zachariah Branch (hamstring) both missed Wednesday’s practice. Dotson is not relevant in 12-team leagues, and Branch has earned just 12 targets this season. Neither player is consequential.

Source: Josh Kendall

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that coach Mike McCarthy “has the full support” of the Steelers’ organization and the team is “not planning to make any immediate changes.”
item.description:
Mike McCarthy PIT Head Coach

McCarthy can rest easy knowing that the organization fully backs him. Rapoport’s “immediate changes” phrasing does allow room for interpretation, though. Perhaps the team could move on in the offseason. Until then, McCarthy will roll with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback. They face the Broncos on Friday.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck has been steadily improving since back spasms hit him late in Thursday’s practice. The team is taking it one day at a time with him. The team is preparing to start Josh Johnson in Week 12 against the Commanders this week.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Cardinals claimed QB Kedon Slovis off waivers.
item.description:
Kedon Slovis ARI Quarterback

The former Raven is now a Cardinal. He was notably on Arizona’s roster last summer. Slovis could end up taking live reps, pending Carson Beck’s (back) health and Josh Johnson’s performance, but he would only be a QB2/3 in that instance.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Chargers claimed CB Avery Smith off waivers.
item.description:
Avery Smith LAC Cornerback

The Chargers traded Smith to the Seahawks earlier this year. The Seahawks waived him on Tuesday. Whether Smith plays meaningful snaps remains to be seen, but he is familiar with the system.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Bengals at this point. The Saints’ No. 1 tight end injured his hamstring last week. Recovering in one week is a tall task for a player who needs to be able to stride while running routes.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was seen practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Taliese Fuaga NO Tackle

Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and C Erik McCoy (biceps) were both practicing on Wednesday. This is great news for the offense overall. Getting both players back would be helpful this week against the Bengals’ talented defensive line.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers has been dealing with this ankle issue for weeks now, but it has not impacted his game-day availability. Meyers is FLEX-viable against a soft Titans pass defense in Week 12.

Source: Jacksonville Jaguars

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate returned from his multi-week absence last week, posting a 2/58/1 receiving line. He faces the Jaguars’ capable defense in Week 12, but his role and talent keep him in the WR3 tier. Tate looks like a classic rookie wide receiver set to produce late in the season.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Abdul Carter (ankle/calf) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Abdul Carter NYG Outside Linebacker

Carter is firmly in the questionable camp for the Giants’ Week 12 game against the lowly Colts. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) was limited at today’s practice. Hopefully, one or both of them are good to go this weekend.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Isaiah Williams (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams missed last week with the rib issue. Omar Cooper was also out, allowing Sterling Shepard to take over the No. 3 receiver role. Shepard saw two targets and managed to get into the end zone on both of them. Cooper appears to be out again this week, but Williams is trending in the right direction. Needless to say, we can’t recommend Shepard (or Williams) in fantasy leagues this week.

item.title: Isaiah Likely (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely injured his groin during practice last week and caught just one pass for 35 yards on Sunday against the Jaguars. His early-week participation is a good sign for his overall health. He will be in the TE1 ranks this week against the Colts.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: D.J. Reed (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
item.description:
D.J. Reed DET Cornerback

Lions EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) and S Chuck Clark (hamstring) are both questionable to play on Thursday. The Lions’ defense was already a fantasy-friendly unit before losing Aidan Hutchinson (knee) for the year. Bears skill position players should be in fantasy football lineups this week.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta began the week with a limited session before upgrading to full on Tuesday. The Lions’ No. 1 tight end should play a full complement of snaps in what will likely be a high-scoring game environment on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Wednesday.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman is expected to return from injured reserve for Week 12 against the Broncos. Two full practices to open the week keep him on track to suit up on Friday. With Aaron Rodgers gone and the Steelers’ receiver room at full strength, Pittman will be a weak FLEX option if activated from IR.

Source: Nick Farabaugh

item.title: Rams activated DT Kobie Turner (groin) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Kobie Turner

Turner missed a month while on IR because of the groin issue. He will be active tonight for a must-win game against the Packers. Turner made six starts this year. He has 22 combined tackles with two passbreakups.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he thinks De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is “a couple of weeks away” from returning.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

Exactly 10 weeks ago, it was reported that Stribling was expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on his ankle. Unfortunately, it sounds like he needs more time to recover. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner believes Shanahan’s comments are in reference to Stribling “returning to practice, not necessarily playing.” Hopefully, Shanahan is actually referring to the latter timeframe. Regardless, Stribling should be stashed on fantasy football benches.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Cowboys activated S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jalen Thompson DAL Safety

Running back Jashaun Corbin was elevated from the practice squad. He will back up Javonte Williams tomorrow against the Eagles. Thompson is back in the lineup after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3. He will provide a small boost to a defense that will need an offseason overhaul to meaningfully improve.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Justin Herbert LAC Quarterback

Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol following the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets. He took eight hits and six sacks that day. Herbert is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. His backup, DJ Uiagalelei, would only be a low-end QB2 against the Patriots if he gets the start this weekend.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is optimistic that Tetairoa McMillan (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

McMillan limped off the field in Week 11 with the foot issue but eventually returned to and finished the game. He did not practice today, though it’s not officially a DNP. The Panthers’ first practice of the week is tomorrow since they play on Monday, which will give McMillan an extra day to recover. Assuming all goes well in practice this week, McMillan will remain a fantasy WR2 for a must-win matchup with the Bucs.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Derrick Henry “had a couple of small symptoms” and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Minter adds that he expects Henry to play in Week 12 against the Texans. On Sunday, it was reported that Henry had cleared the concussion protocol after the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. Re-entering the concussion protocol mid-week seems like a bad sign. Justice Hill has played well in recent weeks and would presumably start in Henry’s stead if the burly back is unable to play. Hill is backed up by Rasheen Ali and rookie Adam Randall, the latter of whom could be worth adding in deep leagues. Henry was limited at practice today.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports the Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers

The team announced his benching late Tuesday night. He then went on The Pat McAfee Show earlier today and burned every bridge in town by saying Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through meetings or missing them outright, among many other accusations. Per Dulac, the interview hastened Pittsburgh’s decision to get Rodgers off the roster. Once he clears waivers, Rodgers will be eligible to sign with another team. It’s unclear if any team will be interested in the Rodgers experience after how things ended in Pittsburgh, but a desperate playoff contender like the Patriots or Ravens could convince themselves of signing him.

Source: Gerry Dulac

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

This is almost certainly just load management for the superstar wide receiver. Evans returned ot action last week, posting a 6/109/1 receiving line. He should be viewed as a talent- and volume-based WR2 against the Seahawks’ top-tier defense. Jordan Watkins (groin) will also sit out on Wednesday.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: Bears ruled out Roschon Johnson (ankle) for Week 12 against the Lions.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

Johnson will be replaced by Salvon Ahmed as the Bears’ No. 3 running back. Ahmed does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, with D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai splitting reps.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Bears ruled out Kyler Gordon (shoulder) for Week 12 against the Lions.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Bears No. 2 perimeter CB Tyrique Stevenson (groin) is questionable to play, which could mean that the Bears are without two of their top-three cornerbacks against the Lions’ elite offense. Tomorrow’s NFC North is looking like a fantasy-friendly environment.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Brock Purdy (ankle) will not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Purdy sprained his ankle in the second quarter of his Week 11 win over the Vikings. He played through the issue but, according to Kyle Shanahan, is now considered day-to-day. With a NFC West bout versus Seattle on tap, we suspect Purdy will play in Week 12 despite the injury. On the other hand, Mac Jones was extremely successful under center last year, so the 49ers wouldn’t be in a terrible spot if they are forced to sit Purdy for a week. Between the injury and the nightmare matchup, Purdy will shuffle to the back of the QB1 ranks this week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: 49ers placed RT Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
item.description:
Colton McKivitz SF Offensive Lineman

This is extremely unfortunate. The 49ers’ talented right tackle is expected to miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The 49ers remain an elite team, but McKivitz’s loss will likely be felt on the field from time to time. The 49ers also activated CB Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and re-signed WR Brandin Cooks to the practice squad.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Week 12 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson failed to practice at any point this week and will miss his second straight game. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be the next man up versus Philly. He caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown last week. “BSF” will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for Week 12.

item.title: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Aaron Rodgers said he issued an ultimatum to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy to give up play-calling duties.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rodgers started off the conversation talking about McCarthy’s shortcomings this year, but he quickly shifted toward accusing McCarthy of being “unwell.” He mentioned several instances of McCarthy missing meetings while sleeping in his office or falling asleep during others. Rodgers also talked extensively about McCarthy failing to stay ahead on film sessions and even brought up a moment on the sidelines when McCarthy broke down the team at halftime with a “1, 2, 3, Packers”. Rodgers feigned concern for McCarthy’s health, though it felt rather disingenuous amidst his scorched-earth campaign. Rodgers told McAfee that he issued an ultimatum to the team to have McCarthy give up play-calling duties. That was seemingly the final straw. Notably, he also talked about being released by the Steelers, though it’s unclear if he has officially made that request. Either way, there’s no coming back from this. He has played his last snap in Pittsburgh. The fact that he’s going out on such a disastrous note means the Steelers won’t want to do him any favors by releasing him. He will likely be inactive and away from the team for the remainder of what Rodgers has said is his final year. If this is the end of his career, it’s a truly unbecoming and sad final chapter for one of the greatest to ever do it.

Source: The Pat McAfee Show

item.title: Woody Marks (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Woody Marks HOU Running Back

Texans reporter Aaron Wilson later added that Marks is expected to return for the team’s Week 12 game against the Ravens. That said, he is unlikely to reliably return FLEX value playing behind David Montgomery. Marks was unable to be a fantasy football difference-maker even when he was operating as the Texans’ starter.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

The Texans could get Harrison back in time for Sunday’s game against the Ravens. While his presence might help CJ Stroud, Harrison can only be viewed as a WR4/5, likely playing in a rotational role on the perimeter. Harrison does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam Darnold (oblique) is expected to start in Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Darnold is expected to practice in full today. He also noted that, as of right now, there’s no quarterback controversy in Seattle. On the other hand, he did mention that the idea of Drew Lock taking over will at least be a talking point if Darnold struggles. For now, it looks like Darnold is back in the QB2 mix for a must-win matchup with the 49ers. We should get confirmation on his health via the team’s injury report throughout the week.

Source: The Pat McAfee Show

item.title: Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, formerly of the 49ers, to the practice squad.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Aiyuk worked out for the Commanders earlier today and they didn’t let him leave the building without a deal. He’ll likely spend a week or two on the practice squad as he gets up to speed with the playbook before being elevated to the active roster. It’s anyone’s guess as to how much Aiyuk has left in the tank. He was struggling early in the 2024 season before suffering a season-ending ACL injury and hasn’t played a snap since. On the other hand, the Commanders need more firepower on offense with Terry McLaurin out for the season and Aiyuk played with Jayden Daniels at Arizona State. The floor is nonexistent, but Aiyuk is still worth adding in deeper fantasy formats.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (Achilles) has not been ruled out for the season.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

This contradicts a report from Ian Rapoport saying that the Colts have decided to shut him down. Pierce suffered a partially torn Achilles in Week 2. He underwent offseason surgery to address his heel/Achilles issues, but apparently it didn’t work. Now Pierce says he’s still hopeful to return later this year. The Colts have already thrown in the towel on the year, trading several big names and cutting Daniel Jones outright. There’s no reason to have Pierce try to play through the issue, so we’re still skeptical that he gets on the field again this year.

Source: Mike Chappell

item.title: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston was held out of the first two practices of Week 11 with the toe issue. He got in a limited session on Friday and played through a questionable tag on Sunday. It’s possible he gets a similar practice regimen this week. Even if he is active again, Boston will be a risky option for fantasy managers. He caught one pass for 16 yards last week and only earned two targets. It’s possible the toe issue is turning him into more of a decoy than a true downfield threat. KC Concepcion would be in line for more work if Boston can’t play at all this week.

Source: Scott Petrak

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert was upgraded to a full practice on Tuesday, meaning he was never at risk of missing tomorrow’s game. Coming off a one-catch bust against the Steelers, things get much better on Thanksgiving for the Eagles’ top tight end. Only four teams are allowing more passing yards per game than the Cowboys. Goedert will be on the TE1/2 border this week.

item.title: NFL agent Drew Rosenhaus said Brandon Aiyuk is having “ongoing and positive” conversations with the Commanders.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Rosenhaus conceded there would “probably” be “no decision today” about Aiyuk joining the Washington roster. That Aiyuk did not sign with the Commanders following Wednesday’s meeting could be bearish for his chances of playing in 2026 at all. Recently released by the 49ers after protracted contract disagreements, Aiyuk would likely start as a rotational player if he eventually signs with Washington.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

It is obviously a poor start to Cooper’s week after he missed Week 11, though coach Aaron Glenn claimed his rookie wideout was “day to day.” That might actually be true, but with the Jets’ season once again lost, we doubt the No. 30 overall pick will be rushed back for a matchup with the lowly Dolphins. Were Cooper to somehow suit up, he would be more of a WR4 than WR3.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith last week dominated air yards and targets in the Eagles offense in his first game back from a two-month hamstring injury. He should be locked into lineups for Thursday’s matchup against the Cowboys. Dallas has allowed the fourth highest EPA per target to wide receivers on the season. Only five defenses allow more expected fantasy points per game to the position.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck, illness) practiced in full Wednesday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley is good to go for Thanksgiving Day against the Cowboys. He left last week’s win over the Steelers with a stinger in the second half but seems OK a few days later. On Thursday he’ll face off against a Dallas defense allowing the second highest rate of fantasy points per touch to running backs, along with the league’s highest rush yards over expected per attempt. Barkley should be considered a locked-in top-12 option.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: The Florida Times-Union’s Demetrius Harvey reports Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was not seen at practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten was banged up last week against the Giants and clearly playing through considerable discomfort. That he hasn’t practiced much over the past couple weeks means Tuten could sit out a couple days of practice this week and still suit up for Week 12 against the Titans. The Jaguars would do well to rest their lead back in a game they should win comfortably. Chris Rodriguez, who bests Tuten in rushing success rate, rush yards over expected per attempt, and EPA per rush, would be in line for a big workload if Tuten is held out in Week 12. Tuten was officially listed as a non-participant on Wednesday.

Source: Demetrius Harvey

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Ken Walker (groin) is out for Week 12 against the Bills.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Walker was always going to be a long shot to suit up for KC’s Thanksgiving night game against Buffalo. This will be the third straight game in which Walker has been sidelined, leaving Emmett Johnson as the team’s workhorse back for at least one more week. Johnson over the past two weeks is fourth in rush yards, ninth in explosive run rate, 14th in rush yards over expected per attempt, and fourth in missed tackles forced per attempt. In other words, he’s good. Johnson will be a top-10 option against the Bills.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Colts DE Caden Curry (wrist) is out for the season.
item.description:
Caden Curry IND Defensive End

Curry suffered the injury last week and will be sidelined for the rest of the season. His absence will be yet another blow for a crumbling Colts defense that has been bludgeoned over the past few weeks through the air and on the ground. Curry had 14 tackles and one tackle for loss over 11 games.

item.title: Bucs opened the 21-day practice window for Jalen McMillan (knee).
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

McMillan has been on injured reserve since late September with a PCL injury. His practice window opening today could mean McMillan will suit up in Week 12 against the Panthers. He would not be a fantasy option for now in a run-first Tampa offense with several wideouts ahead of McMillan in the pass-catching pecking order.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said he expected the Bills offense to be “more complex” in Week 12 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Josh Allen BUF Quarterback

Fowler suggested the Bills kept the game plan as simple as possible last week against the inferior Dolphins, with Josh Allen throwing 45 passes from the pocket and failing to log a single rushing attempt after averaging 7.1 rushes per game coming into Week 11. Fowler said the Bills might have wanted to hide offensive wrinkles ahead of their Thanksgiving night matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The Bills-Chiefs game offers a good fantasy environment and should feature plenty of scoring, though the KC defense allows the second lowest rate of fantasy points per drop back on the season.

Source: NFL Network

item.title: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo said it “sounds like” the benching of Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph was “not a popular decision in the locker room.”
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rodgers was reportedly excused from meetings at the team facility on Wednesday, two days ahead of the Steelers’ Week 12 game against Denver. Rodgers’ benching comes after a series of down games and a proposed change from Rodgers about how plays are communicated to him during the game. Rudolph could be a slight upgrade for Pittsburgh pass catchers and should be rostered in supeflex formats for now.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Rodgers was excused from a Wednesday morning meeting.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Schefter said the veteran was excused from showing up Wednesday morning so he could “process” being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Week 12 against the Broncos. That seems fair. Whatever happens from here, Rodgers has certainly taken his last snap as a Steeler. Rudolph, meanwhile, should be rostered in all superflex leagues for now.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rapoport said McCarthy’s decision came after extensive meetings with coaches, players, and Rodgers himself following the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Joe Milton-led Eagles. Mason Rudolph is slated to get the start in Week 12 against the Broncos. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said the team was set to make a change in play calling, with QB coach Tom Arth relaying plays to Rodgers on game days “at the behest of Rodgers.” Hours later, the 42-year-old veteran was benched. Rodgers had reverted to his 2025 form in the weeks before the benching, ranking 23rd in EPA per drop back and 25th in drop back success rate from Week 8-11. The reuniting of McCarthy and Rodgers in Pittsburgh was always a bit odd considering their falling out in Green Bay. It’s unlikely Rodgers will be on the Steelers roster for much longer now that he has been pulled.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Mason Rudolph PIT Quarterback

The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. Rudolph will oversee an attack that figures to make a sudden swerve to the run, though the 31-year-old with 742 career pass attempts should be able to keep a wideout or two afloat in deeper fantasy leagues. The problem will be figuring out who, as DK Metcalf is having a poor season, Roman Wilson has just returned from injury, and Michael Pittman Jr. will soon join him. Rookie Germie Bernard has been coming in and out of fantasy usefulness, and Pat Freiermuth has caught some passes from Rudolph in the past. In the short term, Rudolph is not a Week 12 streaming option, and only Metcalf can be considered 12-team league viable as we wait to see how things shake out. It is possible, if not likely, the team eventually turns to second-year pro Will Howard or rookie Drew Allar for a late-season evaluation period.

item.title: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worse of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. With the Steelers playing on a short week, they are already issuing injury reports, and Rodgers was not on Tuesday’s edition. It would appear, rather unsurprisingly, the sides have simply soured on each other, an outcome that perhaps became inevitable following Rodgers’ recent downturn. Startlingly immobile, almost anyone would be an upgrade on Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph is really going to push the “almost anyone” framing. Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

item.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports there have “not been a lot of talks about an extension in-season” for Bryce Young.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Wolfe adds that Young and the Panthers are “on the same page for an offseason contract.” Young started out strong this season before a three-turnover loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. The Panthers are still in first place atop the NFC South with a 5-5 record and a second bout with the Bucs on the horizon for Week 12. Young’s extension chances were highly reliant on his play this season but the Panthers need to see more before committing to the 25-year-old quarterback. With a 19-35 record and 67 passing touchdowns to 37 interceptions throughout his career thus far, Young’s performance the rest of this year will determine the status of a contract extension. If the Panthers choose to extend him, it will come in the offseason.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Alex Highsmith PIT Linebacker

Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury.

item.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Quinyon Mitchell PHI Cornerback

Eagles DC Vic Fangio said today he believed Mitchell would be able to go, and it seems like he’s trending in the right direction after hitting the practice field today. It would certainly help anyone facing CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens this week if Mitchell were able to go.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

With the news that Saquon Barkley is practicing in full, Shipley’s waiver wire appeal has downgraded drastically. He’s a reasonable stash and little more at this point in 12-team leagues.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

It’s an upgrade over his limited session on Monday. Barkley told reporters after Sunday’s game that he doesn’t think he’ll ever get to 100 percent again for the rest of the season, saying “That’s not how football works.” But it seems like he’s at least “football healthy” enough to go against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Denver’s Week 12 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant survived an injury scare on Sunday and this confirms that he should be in a good place to play on Friday. He took over as Denver’s No. 2 receiver against the Raiders, out-targeting Courtland Sutton 4-2, but wasn’t able to make much fantasy hay of the increased workload. Pittsburgh should be another game that mostly sees Bryant as a FLEX play at best.

item.title: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly how you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Broncos designated Tyler Badie (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

His 21-day window opens with a full practice. Seems like perhaps J.K. Dobbins’ suspension has accelerated the timeline on this decision, so Badie may have a chance to be activated for Friday’s game against the Steelers.

item.title: Roschon Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

We wouldn’t be surprised if he was an IR candidate after he was carted off during Week 11’s win over the Saints. Salvon Ahmed will likely take over third-string duties for the Bears.

item.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta profiles as a TE1 option in a game with a juicy 55.5 over/under on Thanksgiving. This full session should assure that he skips the questionable line and proceeds directly to a fun game script in the early window.

item.title: Christian Benford (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Benford BUF Cornerback

It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury in Week 10. We had a feeling the Bills would do all they could to have the full roster ready for the Chiefs and it appears Benford will indeed have a chance to suit up.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid talked to reporters after practice and said he is “most likely” playing on Thanksgiving. Not a surprise after a pair of limited sessions, it seems like the Bills simply used their Week 11 game against the Dolphins as an exhibition to rest Kincaid ahead of the Chiefs game. He’ll be on the TE1 line if, as expected, he goes.

Source: Matt Parrino

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday, making him a free agent.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Nobody claimed his 49ers contract. Our next blurb on Aiyuk will probably read something like “Commanders signed WR Brandon Aiyuk,” but until then we’re legally obligated to note that Adam Schefter reported he is expected to draw interest from “a few teams.”

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Bears claimed CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers from the Commanders.
item.description:
Isaac Yiadom CHI Cornerback

Yiadom has been a decent depth corner for most of the last half-decade, but only played on special teams with the Commanders this year. Perhaps the Bears see more in him, or perhaps they just need a gunner.

item.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he suspended J.K. Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

For those of you who haven’t had the pleasure of rostering Dobbins anywhere, know that he played just one snap on Sunday. Whatever went down almost certainly has something to do with that low snap count, though Payton wouldn’t get into it publicly with reporters. If Dobbins could agitate enough to get released, maybe we’d get somewhere in fantasy circles, but as it stands there’s no reason to hold him in shallow leagues.

Source: Nick Kosmider

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

This is at least the start of a movement for Walker to be active for Thanksgiving’s game against the Bills. It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury. His status on Wednesday will be one of the biggest fantasy storylines of the week as it also underscores whether Emmett Johnson will be an RB1 or a contingency FLEX play. It’s hard to read too much into this one way or another, with Andy Reid saying early today that Walker “feels good” probably the best bellwether we have at this point.

item.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

item.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Ben Skowronek PIT Wide Receiver

This could open up more snaps for Pittsburgh’s ancillary receivers even if Skowronek is no fantasy force. He played 10 and 17 snaps in his first two weeks back from the calf injury after he was active for Week 10.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Tuesday.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Mike McCarthy has said he is “very confident” that Pittman will play in Week 12 and this listing does little to douse that. It’s hard to understand if Pittman’s return will actually make Aaron Rodgers target the middle of the field or not, but he would be a rough FLEX play either way in his first game off IR with all 32 teams playing in Week 12.

item.title: Colts signed QB Shane Buechele off the Bills’ practice squad.
item.description:
Shane Buechele IND Quarterback

Buechele got his first NFL experience last year in Week 18, at age 27, when he completed 7-of-14 passes for 88 yards in a game the Chiefs were (probably) looking to lose against the Raiders. He was sacked five times. These last six Colts games will feel like they take five months.

item.title: Ravens waived WR LaJohntay Wester.
item.description:
LaJohntay Wester BAL Wide Receiver

Wester muffed two punts last week against the Panthers, which we’re told is “not a good way to keep your roster spot” when you are here to be the returner. The Ravens will shuffle the deck here.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Packers activated Micah Parsons (knee/PUP) off the physically unable to perform list.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

In other words, the questionable listing from an hour ago does not actually matter. Parsons is back after losing almost a year to a torn ACL. He’ll be directed to put some havoc on the field in his return against the Rams on Wednesday night.

item.title: Steve Avila (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 12 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Steve Avila

Avila did not play in Week 10 and did not practice at all this week coming out of a Week 11 bye. Perhaps the extra rest after this one will get him to a workable place in Week 13. Beaux Limmer started at guard in his place against the Cardinals in Week 10, but with Coleman Shelton (hamstring) also ruled out at center it’s possible that Limmer starts there instead. Bill Murray is the only other interior lineman on the 53-man roster currently, and it’s going to be almost Thanksgiving, not Groundhog Day.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He and Tyler Higbee will both be featured parts of this offense as the Rams look to get by without Puka Nacua. The one that catches a touchdown will be the one that you don’t start.

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

He’ll be good to go against the Packers on Wednesday night. Williams should figure into the high RB2 mix as the Rams try to replace Puka Nacua once again with plenty of split back formations.

item.title: Colts signed OL Wanya Morris off the Cowboys’ practice squad.
item.description:
Wanya Morris IND OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

Jalen Travis and Bernhard Raimann are both dealing with injuries, and other names on the Colts 53-man roster at tackle include Luke Tenuta, Charlie Heck, and Matt Goncalves (a guard for almost the entirety of the year before shifting over in Week 10) as they try to see out the end of this disastrous season. Morris will attempt to see it with them.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

We have no doubts he’ll play — Rams EDGE Myles Garrett said he was able to give Parsons some tickets for the 27-year-old’s long-awaited return yesterday. But players returning from PUP and IR have frequently just gotten a questionable tag regardless of how likely they are to play. Parsons got in limited work in each of the three practices this week.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2.

item.title: Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.
item.description:
Kedon Slovis

He’ll reportedly garner interest from the Arizona Cardinals for some reason. Slovis, 25, played for Arizona in the preseason and the Texans in the 2025 preseason. Over his three preseason stints he’s 86-of-126 for 816 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions while taking nine sacks.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, asked about feeding Omarion Hampton more, said “in hindsight, we should have done that sooner.”
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Many cases of fantasy managers who drafted Hampton in the first two rounds this past August nodding fervently at this news have been reported. Hampton had 15 touches last week and 23 against the Ravens in Week 10. With Justin Herbert (concussion protocol) uncertain for Week 12, it looks like Hampton will be a major part of the game plan yet again against the Patriots.

Source: ProFootballTalk at NBCSports.com

item.title: Browns designated RB Raheim Sanders (hip) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Raheim Sanders CLE Running Back

His 21-day window will open today. Sanders probably won’t come back to a real role unless there are injuries ahead of him, but perhaps he’ll cut into Dylan Sampson’s No. 2 role and make both of them unrosterable.

item.title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Ken Walker (ankle) will participate in practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

“I’m not anticipating a ton of work,” Reid said of Walker, who has missed two straight games and did not practice Monday ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo. “Let’s see how does. He’s feeling pretty good.” If he practices today and Wednesday, Walker should be active for Thursday night. The Chiefs have committed to Walker as the team’s lead back despite Emmett Johnson putting up elite numbers in his absence. Johnson would be startable only in deeper fantasy leagues if Walker is good to go for Thursday.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

He’s headed to injured reserve. Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports DK Metcalf could face fines from the NFL following his Week 11 ejection.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf won’t be suspended for his repeated fights with Eagles defenders on Sunday but he could be fined for the behavior. Metcalf’s meltdown came after he had one catch for two yards in the first half. Among the most inefficient wide receivers in the game, Metcalf has had a disappointing 2026 campaign as the team’s No. 1 wideout. He’ll profile as a flex option in Week 12 against a Broncos defense allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts.

Source: Gerry Dulac

item.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (oblique) would start in Week 12.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.

Source: Pro Football Talk

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. His three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 11, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. Diggs’ veteran presence will need to persist through the uneven quarterback play if the Commanders are to make a push toward the postseason during the final two months of play, a road that was made that much easier with the walk off win over the Bengals. Up next are the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 12, where Diggs will remain a viable Flex play in fantasy.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

item.title: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward.

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

item.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possession before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eke out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. The 4-5-1 Commanders remain two games behind the division-leading Giants with two months remaining in the regular season, but a loss to the Bengals would have made a late-season push toward the playoffs almost insurmountable. Daniels and the Commanders now prepare to face the Cardinals on the road in Week 12, where the veteran signal caller will remain an upside QB2.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. Chase’s next opportunity to flourish comes in a Week 12 meeting with the Saints, where his skillset sets up well to take advantage of one of the highest single-high rates in the league.

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. Joe Burrow fed the running backs and tight ends a massive 24 targets in the face of unrelenting pressure from the Commanders, a situation likely to correct against the single-high-heavy Saints in Week 12, where Higgins returns to WR2 status in fantasy.

item.title: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-6 targets for 77 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Mike Gesicki CIN Tight End

Gesicki saw increased usage against an aggressive Commanders team that brought consistent pressure into the backfield, with the highlight of his game coming on a 32-yard reception over the middle of the field on the team’s final possession, which ultimately ended in a field goal to take the lead with just over two minutes remaining. The Commanders would drive the field and kick the game-winning field goal on the subsequent possession to send the Bengals to 7-3. Gesicki’s weekly volume remains unlikely to approach elite territory, but his elite red zone usage and penchant for finding the paint keeps him in the weekly TE1 discussion in the high-powered Cincinnati offense.

item.title: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 26 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 71 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
Samaje Perine CIN Running Back

The highlight of the game for Perine came on a 44-yard catch-and-run reception where he chipped into a leak route in the flat, springing free from linebacker coverage to give quarterback Joe Burrow an outlet in the face of pressure. He would outrun the secondary and pick up a key block from fellow running back Chase Brown as he sprung free down the sideline for the longest reception in the game. Perine’s 10 opportunities still ranked below the 14 of Brown but the former handily outproduced the presumed starter on his way to a usable fantasy outing. Up next are the ground-funnel Saints, where Perine will return to shaky Flex status in fantasy circles.

item.title: Chase Brown rushed six times for six yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 30 yards on five receptions.
item.description:
Chase Brown CIN Running Back

Brown saw minimal usage in the first half as the two teams played through driving rain, likely equal parts known tendencies as it was matchup-based. The bigger story here was the involvement of Samaje Perine, who did more than his standard change of pace role implied on his way to 97 total yards. There was no mention of injury or anything that would suggest Brown’s role was limited by necessity, likely best viewed as a small blip on the fantasy radar. Brown’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy week comes in Week 12 against the Saints, where he will remain a fantasy RB2.

item.title: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ 22-20, Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow snapped a steak of five consecutive games in which he accounted for four or more touchdowns in the loss. He came into the game tied for the NFL record for consecutive games with four more touchdowns, ultimately unable to move into sole possession in game that played through driving rain throughout the first half. He leaned heavily on his running backs and tight ends against an aggressive Washington defense, feeding the two positions 24 targets on the evening. A defense that was able to stifle the Commanders in the first half allowed five consecutive scoring drives after the break, all of which were field goals, proving enough to send the Bengals to their third loss of the season. Now 7-3 and only one game ahead of the Browns and Steelers, the Bengals suddenly find themselves locked in one of the tighter divisional battles heading into the final two months of the regular season. Up next for Burrow and the Bengals are the Saints in Week 12, where Burrow will remain a top tier QB1.

item.title: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Roschon Johnson CHI Running Back

Johnson departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Saints with an ankle injury and did not return, making his absence Monday notable on the short week. Expect D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to dominate snaps and opportunities out of the backfield for the Bears in one of the biggest games of the season, with the winner left standing alone atop the competitive NFC North.

item.title: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worst of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. With the Steelers playing on a short week, they are already issuing injury reports, and Rodgers was not on Tuesday’s edition. It would appear, rather unsurprisingly, the sides have simply soured of each other, an outcome that perhaps became inevitable following Rodgers’ recent downturn. Startlingly immobile, almost anyone would be an upgrade on Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph is really going to push the “almost anyone” framing. Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

This is at least the start of a movement for Walker to be active for Thanksgiving’s game against the Bills, it’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury. His status on Wednesday will be one of the biggest fantasy storylines of the week as it also underscores whether Emmett Johnson will be an RB1 or a contingency FLEX play. It’s hard to read too much into this one way or another, with Andy Reid saying early today that Walker “feels good” probably the best bellwether we have at this point.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 11 injury report.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He and Tyler Higbee will both be featured parts of this offense as the Rams look to get by without Puka Nacua. The one that catches a touchdown will be the one that you don’t start.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 11 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2.

item.title: Sam LaPorta (ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

The ankle appears to be a non-issue, assuming LaPorta can manage to participate in practice Tuesday. The team will hold two more sessions ahead of Thursday’s divisional showdown against the Bears on Thanksgiving, a game that will decide which team stands alone atop the competitive NFC North with six weeks remaining in the regular season.

item.title: Sam Darnold (quad/rib) was present at practice Monday.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks held their “bonus” practice Monday as they prepare to face the 49ers on the road in Week 12. The level of participation of Darnold is not fully known considering the team does not owe a full practice report until Wednesday, but Darnold’s presence at practice appears to reinforce previous reports that the team expects him to return following their bye. A potential return would be a sizable boost to alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

item.title: Commanders declared CB Amik Robertson, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, RB Robert Henry Jr., Ricky Barber, and G Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Ricky Barber WAS Defensive Tackle

The Commanders host one of the league’s hottest teams as they look to avoid falling further behind in the NFC East. They’ll need their defense to step up against a Bengals team averaging 36.2 points per game during their current five-game win streak.

item.title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, OL Myles Hinton, DL Landon Robinson, OL Dalton Risner, and TE Cam Grandy inactive for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Kyle Dugger CIN Safety

No real surprises here as the Bengals look to continue their string of recent offensive production against an inferior Washington defense. Joe Burrow gets his full compliment of offensive skill position players minus Andre Iosivas, who remains on injured reserve through Week 11.

item.title: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

item.title: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
George Holani SEA Running Back

The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in the league (29), and should see that number creep up a bit with Parsons back in the mix.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly what you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jake Ferguson did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

item.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. The Chiefs didn’t officially practice today, but Walker would not have been present if they did. If he can’t get on the field in even a limited capacity on Tuesday, it would be fair to say he’s trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday’s marquee matchup. If Walker is unable to play, Emmett Johnson would be a fringe RB1 after strong performances in back-to-back weeks.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
item.description:
Quinyon Mitchell PHI Cornerback

It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Broncos designated Tyler Badie (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

His 21-day window opens. Seems like perhaps J.K. Dobbins’ suspension has accelerated the timeline on this decision, so Badie may have a chance to be activated for Friday’s game against the Steelers.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense.

item.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

We described Barkley as leaving the game in the fourth quarter with what “appeared to be a left arm” injury in Sunday’s blurb, it sounds like it may have been a stinger based on the neck listing. A limited (estimated) session is better than a DNP, but Tuesday’s report will loom large for Barkley’s chances of playing against the Cowboys on Thursday.

item.title: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Likely nothing to see here as the veteran tight end prepares for a divisional matchup against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Goedert’s 38-yard reception last week against the Steelers was his longer catch since Week 1, although the fact it was his only grab is troubling considering it was the first game with a healthy DeVonta Smith in a month. Goedert has been relegated to a top end TE2 against the Cowboys.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley should be good to go for the team’s Thanksgiving showdown against the Cowboys Thursday despite the dual-tag designation. The veteran workhorse is coming off one of his best performances of the season against the Steelers, leading the team to their first win in two calendar months.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

item.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DK Metcalf will not be suspended following his ejection from Week 11’s game against the Eagles.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation. While Metcalf denies those allegations, whatever he was attempting to do certainly didn’t look good on tape. While the league has opted not to suspend Metcalf for his actions, he could still face fines for his conduct, which would be handed down later in the week. That said, Metcalf should be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Commanders activated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) off injured reserve.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

“Bill” has missed the minimum four games and was designated as questionable; he has been removed from the injury report by the Commanders and should be their lead back. You likely already had plans to start him if you were holding up your FLEX spot or RB2 position for him, and now you officially can do so.

item.title: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said he doesn’t “necessarily expect to have Jordan Addison (thumb)” back for Week 12 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver
