Addison underwent thumb surgery last week after suffering what was described as a “freak injury” in practice. While he wasn’t considered a candidate for injured reserve, O’Connell did say after the injury that he would likely miss multiple games before returning. If Addison is unable to play in Week 12, it would be the third straight game he has missed with the injury. His practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports RJ Harvey (IR/knee) is “widely expected” to practice when first eligible to come off injured reserve.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey will miss Black Friday’s game against the Steelers, but it sounds like that might be the last one he misses. Jonah Coleman has established a fiefdom at the top of the depth chart in Harvey’s absence, so the second-year back doesn’t necessarily return to a major role in Week 13, but he may be worth picking up in deeper leagues if he was dropped.

Source: Denver Post

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said CB Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
item.description:
Greg Newsome NYG Cornerback

Newsome’s injury comes just weeks after he signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with the Giants. The 26-year-old corner has appeared on 483 defensive snaps this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 71.2 while allowing opposing receivers to catch 19 passes for 209 scoreless yards. His absence will be a tough blow to a Giants secondary that ranks fourth in net yards allowed per attempt and fifth in overall passing yards allowed this season.

Source: Charlotte Carroll

item.title: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is “very confident” Michael Pittman (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman hasn’t played since Week 4 and has put together a forgettable 7-89-0 line in the three games he has suited up for this season. His return comes as the Steelers are in the midst of an offensive slump, as they’ve averaged just 19.3 points per game in their last four games while going 1-3. They’ll need all hands on deck as they prepare to face a tough Broncos defense on Friday.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. The former second-round pick is an explosive playmaker with the ball in his hand and could make for an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy leagues next year once healthy.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
item.description:
Marvin Harrison HOU Wide Receiver

Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice squad. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk

Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. Speaking Monday with the media, Bieniemy said that while Johnson has been impressive in his two games as a starter, the Chiefs “also understand the value [Walker] brings as well.” His practice status will be one to monitor this week, but if he’s active, Walker would be an easy must-start in what could be a high-scoring affair.

Source: Charles Goldman

item.title: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
item.description:
John Lynch SF General Manager

Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. His selection of Brock Purdy as the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft ended up giving head coach Kyle Shanahan his long-term QB of the future after previously failed attempts to address the position post Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick, and in a season where the Niners have been dealt multiple injuries, specifically at receiver, San Francisco currently finds itself with a 9-1 record and three games ahead of the Seahawks and Rams in the NFC West. It’s a much-deserved extension for Lynch, who again has his team on track to make a deep run in the postseason.

Source: Jay Glazer

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks, who is on injured reserve due to a groin injury, has eight days to be activated or lost for the season. The 23-year-old back practiced in full last week all three times only to not be activated. It would be great news for Chuba Hubbard if this continued, as the team has shown little interest in using Etienne in a real role in the backfield.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
item.description:
Tommy DeVito NE Quarterback

After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. Vrabel praised DeVito for the improved play he showed in training camp and the preseason and expressed confidence in him to lead the offense and run the huddle. DeVito hasn’t started a game since the 2024 season with the Giants and has a career passing line of 1,490-9-4 in 15 career games. He threw for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in relief if Maye in Week 10, but will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/Superflex leagues next week against the Chargers.

Source: Mass Live

item.title: Cardinals fired DC Nick Rallis.
item.description:
Nick Rallis

Rallis, whose unit had allowed 323 points in 11 weeks, more than anyone but the Raiders, will give way to interim DC Teryl Austin. Still just 33, there’s a chance the ultra-aggressive Rallis will get another opportunity in this post down the line. Weirdly, the defense hasn’t been the No. 1 problem area in Arizona lately — though that’s certainly more about quarterback attrition than anything — but it’s hard to say that Rallis ever produced a notably above-average unit in three-and-a-half years in the desert. The Cardinals best finish over that span was 14th in DVOA in 2024.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out.

Source: Mia O’Brien

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
item.description:
Seth McGowan IND Running Back

McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans.

item.title: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
item.description:
Daniel Jones

The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. As Rapoport pointed out on Monday on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, “someone, some playoff-ready team unfortunately is going to lose a quarterback at some point,” which could open the door for Jones to join a legitimate contender over the final stretch of the season and ahead of the playoffs. It was reported earlier that the Patriots and Ravens could be interested in Jones, but both teams would be on the outside looking in if the postseason began today. Jones struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts, throwing for 1,974-7-13 in 11 games, but he would likely be an upgrade over several teams’ backup QBs if a starter goes down.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Colton McKivitz SF Offensive Lineman

If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks.

item.title: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Keenan Allen SF Wide Receiver

Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. As is typically the case, Evans caught numerous key passes on third down to extend drives, using his large frame to great effect on both slants and on the perimeter. His touchdown was a fade to the corner of the end zone, highlighting the full range of his talents against a formidable opponent. Fantasy managers will want to track his practice availability in the coming days, but it appears likely Evans can be inserted into lineups as a viable WR1 when the 49ers take on the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival Seahawks.

item.title: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 21-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. The former Mr. Irrelevant tossed three touchdowns for the second consecutive game and the fourth time this season, keeping him in the QB1 ranks in fantasy ahead of another stiff test against the Seahawks in Week 12.

item.title: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined.

item.title: Tai Felton caught 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Tai Felton MIN Wide Receiver

Felton operated as a starter on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson but was unable to capitalize on a team-leading 12 targets. Even so, Felton should be expected to continue as a starter in the offense for as long as Jordan Addison remains sidelined due to a thumb injury, a role that could yield viable Flex status in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers in a bind could do worse than scooping Felton from waivers ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson caught 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

The highlight of the game for the veteran tight end was a posterizing catch down the sideline for a 20-yard gain on the team’s opening possession, a drive that resulted in the first of two missed field goal attempts. Hockenson would play the role of Mr. Reliable from that point forward, although his seven targets finished third on the team behind Justin Jefferson and Tai Felton. The Vikings get the 3-7 Falcons at home in Week 12, where Hockenson will remain a volume-driven TE1.

item.title: Justin Jefferson caught 7-of-9 targets for 86 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding one yard on one carry.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Kirk Cousins and Kevin O’Connell did what they could to get Jefferson involved early and often, although his nine targets ended second on the team behind Tai Felton’s 12. His lone mistake in the game was a costly one, with Jefferson losing a fumble with the team driving on their first possession of the second half down 28-10. The team would not recover after the untimely error, failing to add additional scoring while turning the ball over twice on downs during their subsequent three possessions. Jefferson is clearly in better hands with Cousins under center, a situation that should hold moving forward despite the veteran signal caller being replaced late in a lost game. Fantasy managers can start Jefferson with confidence as an upside WR2 against the Falcons in Week 12.

item.title: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding 13 yards on one reception.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones continues to cede primary rushing duties between the 20s to Jordan Mason but scored for the second consecutive game. After serving as a workhorse back with Mason on the shelf, Jones has not seen more than 11 carries since Mason returned in Week 7, having been held to eight carries or fewer in four of five games. That leaves very little room for fantasy upside on the worse side of a true timeshare, meaning fantasy managers are better off leaving Jones on their bench ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: Jordan Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, losing one yard on one reception.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason led the team in rush attempts and yardage while ceding high-value touches to Aaron Jones for the second consecutive week, with the latter accounting for the only touchdown scored by the Vikings in the loss. The poor game environment and inability of the offense to sustain drives led to the modest touch total for the veteran back, who has become a difficult player to trust in fantasy circles given the current split in workload. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

item.title: Kirk Cousins completed 26-of-38 passes for 235 yards and one interception in the Vikings’ 35-10, Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins MIN Quarterback

This one started with all the makings of a true shootout, with the two teams trading blows early to push the score to 14-10 in favor of the 49ers through the first six possessions. That would be where the offensive production stopped for the Vikings, who turned the ball over twice and missed two field goals. We’ll give a pass on the second field goal attempt missed considering it came up just feet short of setting a new NFL record at 71 yards in the altitude in Mexico. The tires became entirely deflated for the Vikings after a Justin Jefferson fumble halted any momentum coming out of the half while trailing 28-10. A touchdown on that drive makes it a game, but the Vikings ultimately failed to muster any additional scoring after their third possession of the game. Cousins ended up giving way to Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter in a lost game after failing to throw for a touchdown for the first time this season. The 7-3 Vikings get a full week to prepare for the Falcons in Week 12, where Cousins will return as an upside QB2.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 61 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Sean Payton tried to get Waddle going as a deep option today with mixed results. Waddle gained at least 18 yards on all three of his catches. He was also held to just three catches. Waddle has caught more than five passes in one game this year. Today was just his second outing over 50 yards. Waddle isn’t completely useless for fantasy purposes, but the case for him as a WR3 grows worse by the week. With no teams on bye in Week 12, Waddle will finally hit the WR4 ranks versus Pittsburgh.

item.title: Courtland Sutton did not catch either of his targets in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Courtland Sutton DEN Wide Receiver

Sutton posted a solid 5-45-1 receiving line before the Broncos’ Week 10 bye, but it felt like the team was ready to move Pat Bryant into a larger role. Bryant only managed four targets, but it was his first time seeing more looks than Sutton all year. He caught three of them for 32 yards. Now facing increased competition for opportunities, Sutton’s fantasy outlook is going from bad to worse headed into Week 12. He will be a touchdown-or-bust WR5 versus the Steelers.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-10 targets for 84 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was second on the team in targets and receiving yards, trailing Parker Washington’s eight catches for 103 yards. Meyers’ 26-yard grab was the biggest play of the day for the Jaguars, who were forced into a pass-heavy chase script in the second half — a rarity for Jacksonville. Meyers will be a passable WR3 play in Week 12 against the Titans. He had 34 yards on three catches against the Titans in Week 10.

item.title: Pat Bryant caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant got off to a hot start with a 20-yard grab on the Broncos’ opening drive. That would account for over half of his production on the day as Bo Nix could not get any of his receivers going. Bryant still finished second among the team’s wideouts in targets, though Evan Engram and Jonah Coleman both saw more opportunities in the passing game than him. Bryant also survived an injury scare late in the game. His leg got rolled on during a tackle in the fourth quarter. He tried to get up but went back down on the field. Bryant walked off under his own power, worked through the issue on the sideline, and returned a few plays later. We expect to see him on the injury report, but he should be available for Week 12. He will be in the WR4 mix versus Pittsburgh.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez had four rushes for 28 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 13 yards.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

C-Rod handled a limited workload again, even despite Bhayshul Tuten coming on and off the field with ankle and knee injuries that have slowed him down of late. Tuten ended the game with ten carries and three receptions. Rodriguez could have a valuable workload in Week 12 against the Titans if the Jaguars rest Tuten for the stretch run. Rodriguez should be rostered in all formats as a solid contingency option.

item.title: Evan Engram caught 6-of-8 targets for 74 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Evan Engram DEN Tight End

Engram was surprisingly involved in this game, and not just on check-downs. Four of his catches went for at least 10 yards, propelling him to a season-high in receiving yards. The only downside to his performance was the lack of a touchdown. That went to Adam Trautman on a short goal-line toss. While Engram’s pop-up game might help some best ball players, it’s not worth chasing headed into Week 12 against the Steelers.

item.title: Josh Cameron caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Josh Cameron

Cameron ran only 22 routes on 56 Jacksonville drop backs but was second behind only Parker Washington (12) in targets. Cameron will be a borderline fantasy option next week against a terrible Titans secondary. Cameron had 67 yards on three catches against Tennessee in Week 10.

item.title: Brian Thomas caught 1-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Thomas, who ran a pass route on 33 of the team’s 56 drop backs, caught his first touchdown since Week 8 and only his third score of the year. His route involvement saw a bump over Josh Cameron, who had been playing more than BTJ. Cameron had just 21 routes on the day and caught three balls for 44 yards. Thomas was among the Jacksonville pass catchers who benefited from the game’s inflated volume. He’ll be a high variance flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

item.title: J.K. Dobbins rushed one time for zero yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Jonah Coleman completed his takeover of the backfield today with 24 carries, four catches, and three touchdowns. Dobbins, meanwhile, saw as many carries as Cody Schrader. Dobbins’ carry total has gone from seven to four to one in his past three appearances. Sean Payton has decided that this is Coleman’s backfield and there’s not much Dobbins can do about it. Fantasy managers can cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

item.title: Bo Nix completed 19-of-35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 38-24, Week 11 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Bo Nix DEN Quarterback

Nix got on the board early with a goal line toss to Adam Trautman, but it was all Jonah Coleman after that. The rookie running back punched in three rushing touchdowns, all from no farther than seven yards out. Nix did have several close calls on the day. He threw a well-placed deep ball to Troy Franklin, and the pass simply doinked off his helmet. Franklin was laying out for the ball, so it may not have been a touchdown, but it still would have juiced Nix’s box score. Nix also threw a dime to Marvin Mims on a flea-flicker that went down to the one-yard line. He was then stuffed on a sneak, after which Coleman made it into the end zone. All in, it was a better performance from Nix than the box score suggests. With no teams on bye next week, Nix will likely be relegated to the top of the QB2 ranks for his date with the Steelers.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught all three of his targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange didn’t see much involvement in a game that saw Trevor Lawrence attempt a season-high 47 passes, though he ran a route on 44 of the team’s 49 drop backs. Strange, who has more than five targets in five games this season, will be a fine fantasy option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that ranks among the most generous to enemy tight ends.

item.title: Michael Mayer caught 1-of-4 targets for four yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

To add insult to injury for fantasy managers who streamed Mayer, Ian Thomas found the end zone on his only grab of the day. Mayer has typically played the inline tight end role with Brock Bowers operating as a de facto wide receiver. Because of that, Bowers’ absence today didn’t actually free up that many extra snaps or routes for Mayer. The targets also went to the team’s wide receivers instead of Mayer. Whether or not Bowers plays next week doesn’t make much of a difference for Mayer. He will be, at best, a low-end TE2.

item.title: JJ McCarthy completed 18-of-38 attempts for 173 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding seven rushes for 33 yards.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

McCarthy looked out of sorts from start to finish. He airmailed a few routine throws and made some questionable decisions from the pocket against a stingy Jacksonville defense. He finished the game 15 percent below his expected completion rate and with a negative EPA per drop back. McCarthy fed Malik Nabers, who managed 55 yards on a dozen targets. He should be a decent streaming option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that has been among the league’s worst over the past month, though Jameis Winston’s tush push involvement has negatively impacted McCarthy’s weekly fantasy prospects.

item.title: Kimani Vidal rushed seven times for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
item.description:
Kimani Vidal LAC Running Back

Keaton Mitchell’s knee and back injuries allowed Vidal to play a little more often on passing downs. Vidal had a five-yard catch called back due to a penalty, and he was given a carry from the Jets’ eight-yard line. He got open on 2nd-and-goal, a few yards shy of the end zone, late in the game, but Justin Herbert unsuccessfully tried to force a throw to Quentin Johnston in the back of the end zone. Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Vidal could warrant FLEX consideration against the Patriots next week, but Mitchell and Herbert’s health will factor into things.

item.title: Colton McKivitz (leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Colton McKivitz SF Offensive Lineman

McKivitz was rolled up on from behind and his leg did things it should not do, with the gruesome injury almost assuredly going to end his season. The veteran right tackle had become a staple for the 49ers before his injury, with the team now forced to shuffle things up front for the remainder of the season. Expect updates from the team in the coming days.

item.title: Jack Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

Bech quietly led the Raiders with seven targets last week but failed to do anything with the sizable role. Though he came up one target shy of the team lead this time around, Bech was the Raiders’ most productive wide receiver or tight end by a wide margin. Fernando Mendoza consistently found him for chunk gains, with four of his grabs resulting in either a first down or a touchdown. Bech’s second score of the year came on a seven-yard out near the goal line. He was initially ruled down at the one, but an expedited review put him on the board. Bech’s role will take a hit if Brock Bowers is able to play in Week 12, but he’s at least challenging Tre Tucker for the WR1 role. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for his Week 12 game against Cleveland.

item.title: Devin Singletary had one rush for five yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding one catch for five yards.
item.description:
Devin Singletary NYG Running Back

Singletary was strictly in a breather back role behind Cam Skattebo, who struggled to get anything going against the Jags. Singletary won’t have any fantasy value unless or until Skattebo misses time in the coming weeks.

item.title: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 89 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding one reception for four yards.
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Hampton ripped off a 30-plus-yard run for the second time in three weeks today, averaging 6.4 yards per carry. He is the Chargers’ best runner, but frequent losing game scripts make his rushing workloads somewhat unreliable. The Chargers called an option run play for Justin Herbert in the red zone late in the game, with Hampton running a couple yards away from him, but Jets defenders recognized it and shut the play down, erasing Hampton’s potential opportunity to catch a pitch and run it in. Keaton Mitchell suffered back and knee injuries and departed early. Justin Herbert entered the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Hampton could warrant RB2 treatment against the Patriots next week, but both injuries will impact his projection.

item.title: Cam Skattebo had 14 rushes for 34 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding three catches for 14 yards.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

It was not the most efficient outing for the backflipping Skattebo, who averaged a meager 2.8 yards per touch and was regularly stuffed at or near the line of scrimmage against a stingy Jacksonville front seven. He did, however, manage 14 of the team’s 15 running back carries. Devin Singletary was limited to one carry on the day. Skattebo will be a solid RB2 option in Week 12 against a Cowboys defense allowing the second highest rate of fantasy points per touch to opposing running backs this season.

item.title: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Tucker led the Raiders in targets, though several of his looks were uncatchable. He racked up plenty of prayer yards but didn’t do much in the way of actual receiving production. The bulk of his output came on a 39-yard toss from Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. Jack Bech, on the other hand, went for 88 yards and a score on eight targets. With Brock Bowers potentially returning next week, even Tucker’s role as an air yards merchant could take a hit in Week 12. He is likely stuck in the WR5 mix for his upcoming game against the Browns.

item.title: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Malachi Fields NYG Wide Receiver

Fields logged a pass route on 42 of the team’s 47 drop backs and was third on the team in targets behind Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo. He now has just three games with at least three receptions in 2026 as a tertiary part of the New York passing offense. Fields will be a deep league flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell did not return to the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets after suffering a knee injury in the second quarter.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell also suffered a lower-back injury after catching a six-yard pass on the Chargers’ opening drive. He was announced as questionable with the back issue, but was available for kick return duties to begin the following drive. Mitchell disappeared after that and was later announced as questionable to return due to the knee injury in the third quarter. Mitchell does not need to be in 12-team lineups against the Patriots, if active, next week.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers again led the Giants in targets, with no other New York pass catcher seeing more than seven targets on the day. Nabers’ looks were mostly of the dink-and-dunk variety; JJ McCarthy missed his top wideout on a couple easy throws in the second half in a disastrously inaccurate outing for the Giants quarterback. Nabers’ 12 targets were the third most of his 2026 season. The near-total lack of target competition in the New York offense means Nabers has as stable a floor as any receiver in the game. He’ll once again be a top-10 option in Week 12 against the Colts.

item.title: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Jalen Nailor LV Wide Receiver

Nailor was marginally more involved with Brock Bowers out this week, but it wasn’t enough for him to make a dent in the box score. He did score a touchdown late in the game, but Fernando Mendoza was well ahead of the line of scrimmage when the ball left his hands, so the play was removed via flag. Nailor is still operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver behind Jack Bech and Tre Tucker. With a hard ceiling on his target volume, Nailor is not on the fantasy radar for Week 12.

item.title: David Njoku caught 2-of-4 targets for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku injured his shoulder on a 13-yard catch-and-run play on the Chargers’ opening drive, but he managed to play through it, leading his position group in targets along the way. The Chargers unsuccessfully tried to involve Njoku on play-action plays twice, including one at the Jets’ 20-yard line. Charlie Kolar caught one pass for eight yards. Oronde Gadsden did nothing. None of these three are on the fantasy football radar next week against the Patriots.

item.title: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington continued to operate as a change-of-pace back for the Raiders. He only saw two fewer carries than Ashton Jeanty, but the latter earned eight targets and led the team with 90 receiving yards. Washington was not targeted. Without any receiving work to fall back on, Washington is stuck in the RB4 ranks headed into a Week 12 matchup with Cleveland.

item.title: Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, adding five catches for 90 yards.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Jeanty broke his first carry of 20 or more yards on a 46-yard sprint into the red zone in the second quarter. The Raiders’ offensive line finally cleared a lane for the former No. 6 overall pick and he ran to daylight before being tracked down by a pair of Broncos defenders inside the five. Per Next Gen Stats, he hit 21.4 MPH on the run, which goes down as his highest top speed since being drafted. Jeanty was also productive through the air. His highlight of the day was a 68-yard receiving touchdown. He beat his man on a wheel route and Fernando Mendoza hit him in stride for a massive score. It was enough for Jeanty to lead the Raiders in receiving for the second straight week. Jeanty’s elite receiving role alone will keep him in the middle of the RB2 ranks for his Week 12 date with the Browns on Sunday Night Football.

item.title: Ladd McConkey caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey mostly ran short-to-intermediate routes from the slot today. Although he dropped what might have been a first-down pickup on the first drive after halftime, he made the most of his other opportunities. McConkey scored an 11-yard touchdown via an out route early in the fourth quarter, faking an in-breaker that left his coverage defender in the dust. McConkey scored again with roughly two minutes left, shaking Jets LB DeMario Davis on a six-yard hitch-and-go before snagging Justin Herbert’s throw in the end zone. It was an encouraging performance for the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver. Unfortunately, the team announced post-game that Herbert has entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Herbert is active, McConkey will be back in the WR2 tier next week against the Patriots.

item.title: Braelon Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for nine yards.
item.description:
Braelon Allen NYJ Running Back

Allen racked up 17 touches in the No. 2 role behind featured starter Breece Hall. The Jets leaned heavily on their backfield today, with Geno Smith playing through an ankle injury. The coaching staff repeatedly called Allen’s number on multiple drives, allowing their burly backup to wear out Chargers defenders. Allen sealed the game with a 15-yard run up the middle, barreling through contact along the way. Allen must be rostered in all fantasy football formats as an elite bench stash at worst. He warrants FLEX consideration next week against the Dolphins.

item.title: Breece Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding three receptions for 14 yards and one touchdown.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

The Jets’ coaching staff designed a run-heavy game plan with Geno Smith (ankle) playing through an injury. Hall and Braelon Allen split 40 touches between the two of them. Although Allen should be expected to remain regularly involved, and even got a little work inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, the Jets made sure Hall was in the game when they got near, or inside, the Chargers’ 10-yard line. Hall scored on 2nd-and-goal from the Chargers’ seven-yard line by running a route across the backfield, behind the line, before catching a pass in the flats and turning upfield for the score. Hall is an RB1 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

item.title: Fernando Mendoza completed 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 38-24, Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Fernando Mendoza LV Quarterback

Mendoza got off to a dreadfully slow start. The Raiders’ first three drives amounted to 11 net yards and a trio of punts. Mendoza was already down 17 by the time he got the ball back for his fourth series. Mendoza then finally settled in and moved the ball well. His first career passing touchdown came on a well-thrown wheel route to Ashton Jeanty. He led his running back to space and Jeanty did the rest. Mendoza tossed two more scores in the second half, but his comeback bid came to a screeching halt with a fourth-quarter pick-six. Broncos corner Ja’Quan McMillan jumped the route and rather easily took the interception to the house. Things get much easier for Mendoza in Week 12 when he takes on the Browns next week. He will be near the back of the QB2 mix for his third start.

item.title: Mason Taylor caught 2-of-2 targets for 25 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Taylor made a nice, leaping grab for 19 yards on the Jets’ third drive before chipping in with a six-yarder on the next drive. He is a reliable starter in real life, but tougher to trust in fantasy football. He is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Dolphins next week.

item.title: Kenyon Sadiq caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

The rookie tight end got going with a nine-yard catch between the hashes on the Jets’ second drive. He showed up again on the third drive, snagging a sidearm throw from Geno Smith behind the line of scrimmage before turning upfield and weaving through traffic for a 10-yard gain, bringing the offense into the red zone. He made a similar play on the fourth drive, taking a shallow crosser for 11 yards. Sadiq continues to flash intriguing post-catch traits while splitting time with Mason Taylor. Sadiq is stuck in the TE2 tier, but should play efficiently against the Dolphins next week.

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic about Brock Bowers’ (ankle/quad) availability for Week 12 against the Browns.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Kubiak told reporters post-game that Bowers continues to make progress as he rehabs his two injuries. Bowers’ backup, Michael Mayer, caught just one pass for four yards today and picked up a back injury along the way. Hopefully, one or both of them will be good to go next week. Stay tuned.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Parker Washington caught 8-of-17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
item.description:
Parker Washington

Washington should have been credited with a touchdown on a gorgeous end zone throw from Trevor Lawrence but the refs for some reason called it incomplete after a lengthy replay review, befuddling even Gene Steratore. This was the rare negative game script in which Parker could flex his statistical muscles as the Jags’ clear WR1, as the usually-balanced Jacksonville offense tilted pass heavy while chasing points in the second half. No other Jacksonville pass catcher had more than ten targets on the day. Washington will be an elite fantasy option in Week 12 against a wretched Titans secondary that gave up 152 yards and a touchdown to Parker in Week 10.

item.title: Isaiah Likely caught 1-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Likely was invisible for most of the game and finished fourth in targets on the day. Along with most other New York pass catchers, Likely suffered from JJ McCarthy’s stunningly inefficient outing in which he was 15 percent below his expected completion rate and averaged a mere 4.6 yards per attempt. Better days are likely ahead for the Giants tight end, including in Week 12 against the Colts.

item.title: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

Johnston’s day was mostly quiet, although he did technically earn an end zone target on the Chargers’ sixth drive. The coaching staff tried to involve his post-catch skill set via a trick-play toss, but he was stuffed at the line of scrimmage. Johnston will be a shaky FLEX option against the Patriots next week, even if Justin Herbert clears the NFL’s concussion protocol.

item.title: Tre’ Harris caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

Harris snagged a 22-yard pass against busted coverage in this one, but that was not his most consequential play. On the Chargers’ third drive, Harris ran a go route inside the red zone and managed to get behind his coverage defender. Justin Herbert uncorked it, and Harris dove for it, but unfortunately, the pass bounced off his hands in the back of the end zone. Jets EDGE David Bailey committed a roughing the passer penalty on the play, which the Chargers accepted, erasing it from the box score. Harris is a boom-bust FLEX against the Patriots next week, pending Justin Herbert’s (concussion) availability.

item.title: Sterling Shepard caught 2-of-2 targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Sterling Shepard NYJ Wide Receiver

The Jets’ practice squad veteran seized the moment with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) sidelined today, scoring twice against the Chargers. The first was a sliding scramble-drill snag in the front of the end zone. On the second, Sterling ran a shallow crossing route from the right slot, caught the pass, turned upfield and simply outran Chargers CB Donte Jackson. Shepard is not on the FLEX radar next week against the Dolphins.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten had ten rushes for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants, adding three catches for 20 yards.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten came into the game with ankle and knee injuries and was hobbled throughout. He was spotted on the stationary bike a couple times in the first half and limped to the sideline a few times in the third quarter. Clearly nowhere close to 100 percent healthy, Tuten ceded five backfield touches to Chris Rodriguez, who was much more efficient with his opportunities (averaging seven yards per carry). The Jaguars could consider resting their lead back in Week 12 against the Titans. If he plays, Tuten will be a top-15 option.

item.title: Adonai Mitchell caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell bagged a 21-yard catch via a corner route on the opening drive. He should have bested it with a 40-plus-yard touchdown catch on the Jets’ fifth drive via another corner route, but Geno Smith overthrew him. Brutal. Mitchell’s downfield role lends itself to volatility, but there’s not much more he could have done there. He had his coverage defender beat. Mitchell remains a volatile yet capable FLEX option in Week 12 against the Dolphins.

item.title: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson generated a decent amount of his receiving yardage after the catch today. He spun off contact and broke another tackle on his 19-yard gain, and also added yards after the catch on a 12-yarder. His first incompletion was a shallow crosser on third down from the Chargers’ 32-yard line, which his coverage defender deserves credit for breaking up. The second incompletion was a desperation heave by Geno Smith under pressure from the Chargers’ six-yard line. The ball was badly overthrown to Wilson, just in front of the end zone, though. He had no chance of catching it. Wilson is a WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

item.title: Geno Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 27-24, Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description:
Geno Smith NYJ Quarterback

The Jets dialed up a run-heavy game plan with Smith playing through an ankle injury suffered last weekend. The ailment didn’t stop Smith from playing efficiently against the Chargers, though. Smith linked up with Breece Hall and Sterling Shepard (twice) for touchdowns today. Smith overthrew Adonai Mitchell on what could have been a 40-plus-yard end zone target, but luckily, Breece Hall ripped off a 26-yarder that set up one of Smith’s touchdown passes to Shepard, who was elevated from the practice squad this week. Smith warrants QB2 treatment against the Dolphins in Week 12.

item.title: Makai Lemon caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
Makai Lemon PHI Wide Receiver

Lemon was a distant afterthought in the Philly offense with DeVonta Smith returning from a hamstring injury and leading the team with 12 targets (57 percent target share). Lemon should not be rostered in most fantasy leagues for the remainder of the season unless Smith again misses time.

item.title: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ 24-27, Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding eight rushes for 32 yards and one touchdown.
item.description:
Justin Herbert LAC Quarterback

Immediately after the game, the Chargers announced that Herbert had entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. He took six sacks and eight hits, including one that resulted in a roughing-the-passer penalty after David Bailey hit him in the facemask while trying to disrupt a pass. Bailey had a field day aside from that, registering two quarterback hits and two sacks while forcing a fumble during one of the latter plays. Fortunately for Herbert, an offensive lineman recovered possession. Herbert’s connection with Ladd McConkey improved as the game progressed, leading to two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. Herbert also audibled to a quarterback-keeper from the Jets’ 10-yard line earlier in the game, which he successfully converted for a score. He notably had his left index finger taped up after halftime. If active next week against the Patriots, Herbert will be a high-end QB2. He is backed up by DJ Uiagalelei.

Source: Noah Furtado

item.title: Jake Elliott made all four of his field goal attempts in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
Jake Elliott PHI Kicker

Elliott also made his lone extra point attempt in the victory. Elliott drilled a couple long kicks through the wind in Philadelphia as he continued a solid 2026 campaign. He’s made 11 of his 12 field goal tries on the season. Sunday marked the first time in 2026 in which Elliott made more than two field goal attempts in a game. He’ll be a decent fantasy option in Week 12 against Dallas.

item.title: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR Jordan Addison, CB Isaiah Rodgers, QB Max Brosmer, and S Jay Ward inactive for Week 11 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

Addison will miss his second consecutive game while the team gets Jauan Jennings back from his own two-game absence. Expect Tai Felton and Myles Price to fill in for Addison while addition volume remains most likely to concentrate on Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson.

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) is active for Week 11 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans returns from three missed games due to an aggravation of the Achilles injury that has plagued him throughout the season, and while he could see his snaps and routes managed, he brings a fantasy WR2 profile to the table in a difficult matchup against the Vikings. Fantasy managers likely did not start him considering the timing of the game this week, hoping he simply makes it through Week 11 healthy. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, DE Khalid Kareem, WR Demarcus Robinson, and LB Dre Greenlaw.

item.title: Adam Butler (concussion) will not return to the Raiders’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
item.description:
Adam Butler LV Defensive Tackle

Fellow defensive tackle Tim Keenan (knee) is also done for the day. The Raiders were already one of the best matchups for running backs entering Week 11. Expect the Broncos to lean on Jonah Coleman to close this game out.

item.title: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Gunnar Helm TEN Tight End

14 of Helm’s 23 catches on the year have come in the past four weeks. It’s been a good start for a second-year pro trying to create some TE2 relevance but not really enough, even in a down year for the position. With all 32 teams active for Week 12 and bye weeks lingering on for only two more Sundays after that, Helm is facing long odds of becoming 12-team league relevant.

item.title: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Elic Ayomanor TEN Wide Receiver

The three-catch effort was Ayomanor’s fourth straight, though he has exceeded three just once during that timespan. He is also averaging only 46 yards in the process, and has not found the end zone. Translation, Ayomanor’s play has been better, but not better enough you are seriously considering him as a WR4. That is especially true for slates like Week 12 where all 32 teams will be active.

item.title: Calvin Ridley caught 5-of-6 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

Ridley entered the game with only six catches for 91 scoreless yards on the season, so he nearly doubled his 2026 production. The highlight was a 12-yard touchdown in garbage time that just happened to be one of the most insane throws of the year. Rolling near the sideline, Cam Ward made a cross-field, cross-body pass to find Ridley on the opposite side of the field in the end zone. It was an easy catch. Good stuff, though nearly all of Ridley’s production came with the Titans down multiple scores in the fourth quarter. The offense is playing better, but not better enough that Ridley is set to return to 12-team league relevance.

item.title: Darius Cooper caught 4-of-5 targets for 59 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
Darius Cooper PHI Wide Receiver

Cooper led all Eagles pass catchers in catches and receiving yards on a day that saw Joe Milton throw just 21 passes in a run-heavy game. Cooper played a full-time role because Dontayvian Wicks remained sidelined after practicing over the past week. Cooper would profile as an interesting flex play next week against Dallas if Wicks remains out.

item.title: Juwan Johnson failed to catch his lone target in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson saw just one target before exiting in the second half of the Saints’ Week 11 game against the Bears. He did not return to the game and head coach Kellen Moore said the 30-year-old is still being evaluated with a hamstring injury. Johnson has not exceeded three targets for five straight weeks now. He can remain on waiver wires moving forward, though Noah Fant enters the streaming conversation if Johnson misses any time.

item.title: Chimere Dike caught 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Chimere Dike TEN Wide Receiver

Dike notched a 22-yard gain on a flea flicker on the Titans’ first play from scrimmage and went on to lead the team in receiving as it put up 30 points in a road loss. Good stuff, and Dike’s second pop-up effort in as many weeks, though it was Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley who made the biggest plays. Second-year fourth-rounder Dike has been one of the biggest beneficiaries as fellow sophomore Cam Ward has finally started to play better, but he’s still having a difficult time cracking the top 48 at receiver. That is going to be especially true for Week 12 against the Jaguars as we get a rare November week with all 32 teams actually playing football.

item.title: Noah Fant caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Noah Fant NO Tight End

Fant was the Saints’ leading tight end on the day, seeing the most snaps, targets, and receptions in the tight end room. He saw a pair of red zone targets in the fourth quarter, though Tyler Shough could not connect with him and the drive ended in a turnover-on-downs. Juwan Johnson is his primary receiving competition, but Johnson saw just one target before exiting with a hamstring injury. No Saints tight end needs to be started for fantasy purposes at this point; Fant is in the streaming tight end conversation should Johnson miss any time.

item.title: Ted Hurst caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Ted Hurst TB Wide Receiver

Hurst brought down a beautiful deep shot right in the bread basket with four seconds left on the clock in the second quarter. He double-dipped near the end of the fourth quarter with a quick out at the goal line for his second touchdown of the day. Hurst led the Bucs in all receiving categories, including a 21 percent target share. Hurst has been a boom/bust receiver this year who mostly gives fantasy managers busts, but his Week 11 breakout gives him something to build on. He will be a high-risk FLEX play when the Bucs take on the Panthers next week.

item.title: Devaughn Vele caught 7-of-7 targets for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Devaughn Vele NO Wide Receiver

Vele saw a decrease in opportunities last week with Jordyn Tyson’s activation off injured reserve. However, Tyson saw limited usage in Week 11 against the Bears, with Vele leading Saints receivers in snaps and ranking second in targets, receptions, and yards. Fantasy managers should wait to see if Tyson has any injury limitations moving forward, but Vele would be back in the WR3/4 ranks if Tyson is limited for Week 12 against the Bengals.

item.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-2 targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Brevyn Spann-Ford DAL Tight End

The closest thing the Cowboys have to a No. 1 tight end during Jake Ferguson’s ongoing absence, Spann-Ford’s two-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter was just the second of his career. It’s what got the Cowboys to 50 points, which is both cool and also tells you all you need to know about Spann-Ford’s fantasy value. It took the Cowboys running it up late against one of the worst teams in the league for Spann-Ford to find the paint. He remains outside the top 30 in the weekly tight end rankings.

item.title: Ryan Flournoy caught an 11-yard pass in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Ryan Flournoy DAL Wide Receiver

Flournoy had his season-worst outing as the Cowboys had their season-best scoring effort. Go figure. Flournoy’s 11-yard grab came on the opening series only for him to draw zero more targets. That’s a rough development for WR3 desperados with six teams on bye. It is also a faceplant that is unlikely to repeat on Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens posting crazy usage numbers. The problem for Flournoy is, with all 32 teams active for Week 12, there’s simply no real way to get him into fantasy lineups.

item.title: Jordan Tyson caught 1-of-2 targets for 6 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one carry for four yards.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Tyson saw the first offensive touch for the Saints, getting four-yard carry to start things off. He saw just one more touch the rest of the game and was barely on the field for the Saints’ final offensive drive. Though he was cleared off the injury report heading into the weekend, Tyson was dealing with a chest injury last week. Also coming back from a hamstring injury this season, Tyson’s compounding injury list may have played a role in him seeing just half of the offensive snaps against the Bears after getting 13 targets last week. He saw just two targets as Chris Olave took the alpha receiver role back. Fantasy managers should monitor Tyson’s injury status heading into Week 12; he is in the WR3 ranks against the Bengals next week.

item.title: Emeka Egbuka caught 2-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

There’s not much to say here. It’s just not happening for Egbuka this year. He’s struggling to earn targets and doing nothing when the ball comes his way. Ted Hurst broke out with two scores and 56 yards on a team-high 56 yards today. Egbuka watched on with a measly 15 percent target share. He’s averaging a dismal five yards per target and has forced zero missed tackles. Egbuka will tumble into the WR4 ranks for his Week 12 game against Carolina. With no teams on bye, fantasy managers can feel comfortable sending him to the bench next week.

item.title: Darnell Washington caught all three of his targets for 22 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
Darnell Washington PIT Tight End

Washington again ran fewer pass routes than Pat Freiermuth, who caught all five of his targets on the day. Washington won’t have much in the way of fantasy value until or unless Freiermuth misses time. Washington has five games this season with at least three catches.

item.title: Dallas Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert ran a pass route on 20 of the team’s 29 drop backs but only saw one look from Joe Milton, who attempted a meager 21 passes and threw for 141 scoreless yards. DeVonta Smith’s return to the Eagles lineup netted him a 57 percent target share. That kind of target domination won’t leave much opportunity for anyone else, including Goedert, who should not be played in 12-team formats for now. The Eagles play the Cowboys in Week 12.

item.title: Javonte Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans, adding three receptions for 24 yards and a second score.
item.description:
Javonte Williams DAL Running Back

Williams lost some mop-up work to someone named Jashaun Corbin but cleared 20 touches for the fourth time in five games. The touchdowns were his 11th and 12th of the season, and give him 25 in 27 appearances as a Cowboy. Williams continues to not provide efficiency, but that’s not what’s needed opposite the Cowboys’ elite receiver duo. Williams needs to finish drives at the goal line and do a little bit of everything else, and that’s what he has been doing. Williams will be a low-end RB1 for Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles.

item.title: CJ Donaldson rushed one time for five yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding four receptions for 12 yards and a fumble.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

Donaldson is head coach Kellen Moore’s pride and joy as a passing-down back in the backfield. The undrafted rookie continues to run routes despite a lack of efficiency and production all season. He was used as a pass blocker and ran 25 routes on the day, more than rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson. Donaldson fumbled on one of his receptions in the second quarter, totaling 12 yards through the air and five on the ground. He has no fantasy value heading into Week 12.

item.title: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 13 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Chris Godwin TB Wide Receiver

The Bucs leaned on Godwin on third downs, using him to move the chains on two of his three targets. That, however, is a cold comfort for fantasy managers. Godwin hasn’t hit 50 yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown. If you somehow made it this far into the season with Godwin on your roster, it’s past time to cut bait. He’s somewhere beyond the WR5 ranks heading into Week 12.

item.title: Will Shipley had four rushes for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley saw some decent fourth quarter run with Saquon Barkley nursing some sort of left arm injury. Shipley would likely take over the Eagles’ lead back if Barkley were to miss time. He should be rostered in most 12-team formats just in case, considering the Eagles take on the Cowboys in Week 12.

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
Pat Freiermuth PIT Tight End

Freiermuth ran 33 routes on the day while Darnell Washington logged 22 routes and had three targets from Aaron Rodgers. Freiermuth was fourth on the team in targets and receiving yards. Sunday was only the fourth time this season Freiermuth had more than four catches in a game. His waning route participation and the run heaviness of the Pittsburgh offense make Freiermuth nothing more than a desperation option for Week 12 against Denver.

item.title: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard was held without a catch on one target. Frustrating, though fantasy managers will take Pollard’s third 100-yard rushing effort in four weeks considering the Titans were down 27-9 at halftime. Pollard was “keeping the defense honest” as Cam Ward again showed increased play-making ability in the passing game. Pollard has now cleared 75 yards from scrimmage in five straight contests after doing so just once in the first five games of the season. He is amongst a number of Titans just genuinely playing better, though it is still not translating to victories. That will remain a pipe dream for Week 12, but Pollard will be rematching with a Jaguars defense he got for 99 yards from scrimmage in Week 10. It must be noted that was due in large part to a ridiculous eight receptions, which probably won’t be repeated seeing as Pollard has only 22 on the year.

item.title: Alvin Kamara rushed one time for one yard in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one reception for one yard and a touchdown.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara was the third running back in the Saints backfield, seeing just six total snaps. He came in for a fourth-and-goal pay at the one-yard line and caught a Tyler Shough pass for the touchdown. Kamara only received one carry for one yard. The Saints have a frustrating backfield committee, with Travis Etienne getting the bulk of the carries, CJ Donaldson running routes, and Kamara coming in for the occasional red zone target. Three touchdowns in his last two games keeps Kamara on the fantasy radar, though he is close to a zero without the red zone opportunities. Kamara is best left on benches for Week 12 against the Bengals.

item.title: Travis Etienne rushed 14 times for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

The good news is that Etienne started the game for the Saints backfield and received 14-of-16 running back carries. He led the backfield with 21 total snaps as Audric Estime was a healthy scratch against the Bears. Etienne’s best run of the day was a 46-yard carry in the second quarter, where he was chased down and tackled inside the five-yard line. He got two more opportunities and got the ball to the one-yard line, but did not get the touchdown on that drive. Etienne’s lack of passing-game usage and Alvin Kamara’s involvement as a touchdown scorer caps Etienne’s ceiling for fantasy purposes. He belongs in the RB3 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

item.title: Cade Otton caught 1-of-3 targets for eight yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
item.description:
Cade Otton TB Tight End

Otton popped up with a four-catch, eight-target game before the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. He was unable to build on that box score and all but disappeared today. Otton hasn’t topped five catches or 56 yards in a game this year. He has also been held without a touchdown through nearly three months of action. He’s barely even a TE2 for Week 12 against the Panthers.

item.title: George Pickens caught 7-of-10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens got off to a slow start this afternoon, seeming to not finish a route or two, but finished molten hot. He is now up to 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns on 28 targets over the past two weeks. Ridiculous numbers, though somewhat sustainable in this narrow, explosive offense. For Thanksgiving Day he will be rematching with an Eagles defense he got for 4/57/1 last month. The Eagles have moved on to their No. 3 quarterback since then and traded a few key contributors. Even with all 32 teams active for Week 12, Pickens will remain in the low-end WR1 mix.

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding four catches for 43 yards.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Gainwell could see more touches going forward to help keep Bucky Irving fresh. That couldn’t have been further from the truth today as Irving out-touched Gainwell 21-8. Gainwell did, however, post his second-best receiving line of the year. His only better game came two weeks ago, before Tampa’s bye, against the Bears. Gainwell might finally be developing a receptions-based floor, but a two-game sample can’t be taken as gospel. Gainwell will remain on the RB3/4 border when he takes on the Panthers next week.

item.title: Zavion Thomas caught 2-of-3 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for 30 yards.
item.description:
Zavion Thomas CHI Wide Receiver

Thomas was the subject of multiple explosive plays against the Saints. He saw just offensive 10 snaps, but Ben Johnson schemed up multiple plays to utilize the rookie receiver’s speed. A 40-yard reception in the third quarter and 30-yard rush in the second quarter highlighted a career-best day for Thomas. He is still not fantasy relevant, but his usage should be monitored as the Bears scheme up more plays for him.

item.title: Jaylen Warren had nine rushes for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding two catches for one yard.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren was snuffed out by a swarming Philadelphia defense that appeared committed to stopping the Pittsburgh rushing attack and forcing Aaron Rodgers to beat them (he did not). Warren ran 36 routes on the day to Rico Dowdle’s 16 routes, though it was Dowdle who led the backfield with five targets. Warren now has back-to-back down games in a collapsing Steelers offense. Things won’t get much easier in Week 12 against the Broncos.

item.title: Rico Dowdle had five rushes for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding four catches for 19 yards.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Jaylen Warren, meanwhile, managed 29 yards on nine rushing attempts and caught one of his two targets. Dowdle got quite a lot of second half playing time, finishing the game with 16 pass routes to 36 routes for Warren. Dowdle is good for 7-10 touches per week in the low-octane Pittsburgh offense, making him a desperation flex option in deeper formats.

item.title: Kalif Raymond caught 1-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Kalif Raymond CHI Wide Receiver

Raymond was targeted four times, including an incomplete end zone target on fourth down in the first half. He caught one of his targets for 14 total yards, though he had the second-most wide receiver snaps on the team. Raymond is still involved as the starting outside receiver opposite Rome Odunze but has boom-or-bust WR5 viability at best heading into Week 12

item.title: Justice Hill rushed six times for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 27 additional yards.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Hill fell victim to one of the worst rules in football when he fumbled inside the Panthers’ five-yard line on a 36-yard run and watched the ball run out of the end zone.
